articles.title: Black Friday? No thanks, some brands say
articles.summary: Some brands are opting out of Black Friday to protect margins, push back against constant discounting or signal sustainability values. Italian fashion brand Pinko estimates the decision will cost about €2 million in revenue but says the profit hit is smaller. Analysts say discount fatigue and distrust of advertised savings make the strategy risky, though it can help retailers stand out.

articles.title: No. 18 USC rallies, then holds on to edge South Carolina
articles.summary: No. 18 Southern California stayed unbeaten at 7–0 by rallying past South Carolina 71–69 in the Acrisure Series. Alijah Arenas scored 25 points, including 12 of 13 free throws, as USC closed on a 10–2 run and held the Gamecocks scoreless for the final 4:05. South Carolina led by as many as 10 but missed two late go-ahead shots.

articles.title: US judge blocks FCC from threatening Disney-owned ABC stations
articles.summary: A U.S. judge barred the Federal Communications Commission from continuing steps that threaten Disney-owned ABC stations' broadcast licenses, saying the agency appeared to be pursuing retaliation driven by President Donald Trump. Judge Loren AliKhan said FCC Chair Brendan Carr had treated Trump's rhetoric as marching orders. The ruling protects the broadcaster's right to avoid government retaliation for protected speech while the case proceeds.

articles.title: New Trump tariffs would likely increase sugar prices in the US
articles.summary: The administration proposed a $440-per-metric-ton duty on raw sugar imports outside the low-tariff quota, ostensibly aimed at Brazil but applying to other suppliers as well. Analysts estimate the combined tariff on out-of-quota sugar could reach 193%; U.S. March sugar futures jumped 14.65% to 45 cents a pound. Industry groups warn food makers and consumers will face higher costs.

articles.title: International Paper names insider Nicholls CEO of DS Smith spinoff
articles.summary: International Paper named longtime executive Timothy Nicholls to lead DS Smith, its planned spinoff combining the company's Europe, Middle East and Africa packaging operations with the $7.2 billion DS Smith acquisition. The standalone business is expected to list on the New York and London exchanges around December 7. The separation follows board approval earlier this week.

articles.title: Poland's Orlen dismisses CFO, deputy CEO, shares fall
articles.summary: Poland's state-controlled oil refiner Orlen dismissed its chief financial officer Slawomir Jedrzejczyk and deputy CEO Marek Balawejder, sending shares down as much as 4.8%. The company gave no reason, and the Ministry of State Assets declined to explain, saying the supervisory board made the decision. The departures add uncertainty around governance at one of Central Europe's largest energy groups.

articles.title: Tardy batter bowled out without facing a ball
articles.summary: Melbourne Renegades batter Deandra Dottin was timed out in Australia's Women's Big Bash League after failing to reach the crease within a new 75-second limit. Brisbane Heat bowler Sarah Glenn hit the unattended stumps before Dottin faced a delivery. Renegades captain Sophie Molineux said the team made the call too late, calling it an unusual lesson for future matches.

articles.title: Bollywood union asks Modi to bar Netflix's Pakistani series in India
articles.summary: India's All Indian Cine Workers Association urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to block Netflix's Pakistani series 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo,' scheduled for December 4, and called for a permanent law penalizing Pakistani content. The union cited security tensions between the countries. Netflix and Modi's office did not immediately comment; the request could test streaming platforms' obligations in a major market.

articles.title: Brazil announces new credit rules to curb household indebtedness
articles.summary: Brazil's central bank and monetary council announced safeguards to curb household debt. Lenders will be barred from increasing unsecured exposure to customers more than 90 days overdue, and card limits will be gradually reduced for some people who miss full payments on three or more bills in six months. Most measures take effect July 1, 2027, amid high borrowing costs.

articles.title: Andy Taylor, guitarist of new wave icons Duran Duran, dies at 65
articles.summary: Andy Taylor, the guitarist and songwriter who helped shape Duran Duran's early sound, died at 65 after metastatic prostate cancer, his family and bandmates announced. Diagnosed in 2018, he co-wrote major hits including 'Rio,' 'Hungry Like the Wolf' and 'Girls on Film.' Taylor joined the band in 1980, before its international breakthrough with the 1982 album 'Rio.'

articles.title: Biomimetic coacervate lubricant protects OA joints
articles.summary: Nature Reviews Rheumatology describes a biomimetic polyzwitterionic coacervate engineered to restore the lubricating layer that breaks down in osteoarthritis. The material binds cartilage, forms a stable low-friction coating and can deliver therapeutic compounds; experiments found it reduced friction more effectively than clinical hyaluronic acid. It remains experimental, with human safety and benefit unproven.

articles.title: Gut microbes can adapt to our ageing bodies
articles.summary: Nature reports a study of more than 10,000 people that found age-associated genetic changes in gut bacteria, including an adaptation that may help one abundant species resist oxidative stress. Researchers compared microbial variation with nearly 250 human traits and found few mutations associated with disease. The findings suggest microbes evolve within ageing bodies, but do not establish a clinical treatment.

articles.title: BBC lodges urgent appeal against Trump's $10bn defamation lawsuit
articles.summary: The BBC asked the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 11th Circuit to dismiss Donald Trump's $10 billion defamation suit over a Panorama documentary that edited two portions of his January 6 speech together. The broadcaster says the program aired only in Britain and was not accessed in Florida. It apologized for the edit but denies defamation; Trump's deposition was postponed until January.

articles.title: Puerto Rico's Supreme Court cancels a key power contract and many wonder what's next
articles.summary: Puerto Rico's Supreme Court voted 5–4 to cancel the government's contract with LUMA Energy, the private operator of power transmission and distribution. Officials have one year to arrange a successor while outages persist; Gov. Jenniffer González says operations will not return to the public utility. A federal control board warned that no clear transition plan or replacement company is in place.

articles.title: Judge halts order for Georgia's Fulton County to give 2020 election records to state election board
articles.summary: A Georgia judge paused an order requiring Fulton County to give the State Election Board a digital copy of 2020 ballots and related records seized by the FBI, after county officials appealed. The board has sought to reopen election allegations; multiple courts and officials found no fraud that changed the result. The records dispute remains on hold during the appeal.

articles.title: Judge declines to issue a long-term ban on taxpayer-funded, pro-Trump ads critics called propaganda
articles.summary: A federal judge declined to extend a temporary ban on taxpayer-funded advertisements promoting President Donald Trump, ruling the Democratic National Committee had not shown it was likely to prevail after the midterms. The suit challenges at least 11 spots partly funded by a $20 million Homeland Security contract. A separate New York judge ordered three ads removed; the administration calls them public-service messages.

articles.title: New York court upholds Mayor Mamdani's rent freeze
articles.summary: New York’s state Supreme Court upheld Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s rent freeze for rent-stabilized apartments, rejecting landlords’ claim that his appointees compromised the Rent Guidelines Board. The freeze covers about one million of the city’s 2.3 million rental units for leases renewing through Sept. 30, 2027. The landlords argued the process was biased; the judge said they had not shown it was arbitrary or unlawful.

articles.title: Trapped on the Tarmac: 3-Hour Flight Delays Spike Under Trump
articles.source: The New York Times (via GV Wire)
articles.summary: U.S. flights are on pace for their highest number of tarmac delays exceeding three hours since 2009, according to Bureau of Transportation Statistics data cited by The New York Times. The report says the Transportation Department has issued no airline consumer-protection fines in nearly two years, although officials say investigations continue. The delays remain relatively rare but can leave passengers confined aboard aircraft for hours.

articles.title: Study: Climate change driving increased summer thunderstorm activity, flash flood risk in New England
articles.summary: An analysis of 40 years of hourly observations from 80 New England airports found that summer rainfall is increasingly concentrated in shorter, heavier thunderstorms. Researchers reported that storms averaged nearly 40 minutes shorter in 2000–2020, while the most intense downpours made up a 25% larger share of thunderstorm rain. They warn aging drainage systems may face greater flash-flood pressure as the climate warms.

articles.title: UC San Diego Brain Organoids in Space Reveal New Clues to Alzheimer’s Disease
articles.summary: UC San Diego researchers sent Alzheimer’s-modeling brain organoids to the International Space Station for 40 days and found that spaceflight responses differed by genetic background. The models showed distinct changes in disease-related proteins and gene activity, while researchers identified altered stress-response pathways. The findings are preliminary and do not show that spaceflight causes Alzheimer’s, but may help refine laboratory models of the disease.

articles.title: Tiny Robots Deliver Treatments to the Brain
articles.summary: Caltech researchers developed light-activated nanorobots designed to cross the blood–brain barrier and deliver medication. In mouse models of glioblastoma, the system delivered about five times more drug to the brain than nonactivated controls, slowed tumor growth and prolonged survival, while reducing systemic toxicity. The work is experimental; it has not been tested as a treatment in people, and further safety and efficacy studies are needed.

articles.title: ASU scientists create a new way to assemble complex structures at the nanoscale
articles.summary: Arizona State University researchers demonstrated a programmable system in which designed DNA cubes spontaneously assemble into complex three-dimensional structures. The team used computational design to limit assembly errors and built increasingly intricate forms, pointing toward reconfigurable nanoscale devices and 3D circuits. The work is a materials-design proof of concept, not a functioning nanorobot or electronic chip, and practical applications remain developmental.

articles.title: Later-born generations have better memory and lose it more slowly
articles.summary: An analysis of about 219,000 people followed for up to 30 years found that later-born generations entered older age with higher memory performance and experienced slower decline than earlier cohorts. The Nature Medicine briefing says the combined advantage could help explain falling dementia incidence over time. The finding reflects population trends, not a guarantee for individuals, and does not eliminate other dementia risk factors.

articles.title: EU nationals will pay higher tuition fees than UK students, Burnham indicates
articles.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham indicated that EU students will not receive the same domestic tuition rate as British students under a proposed post-Brexit reset deal. Negotiations remain unresolved, with the EU seeking equal treatment and UK universities concerned about losing international-fee revenue. The dispute could complicate parts of the wider agreement, although Burnham said tuition talks were separate from the main package.

articles.title: Japan's data centre boom faces growing revolt from urban residents
articles.summary: Japan’s rapid data-centre expansion is drawing opposition from residents near Tokyo, who cite generator fumes, noise, heat and fuel-storage risks as facilities move close to homes. About 60% of the country’s data centres are in the metropolitan region. The government is preparing an action plan and local guidelines, while residents in several cities seek binding protections and one group has challenged a project’s zoning approval.

articles.title: Australia's Flight Centre probes data breach in third-party system
articles.summary: Australia’s Flight Centre Travel said it was investigating unusual activity in a third-party accommodation-booking system that may have exposed a significant number of customer records. Some leisure brands and independent agents used the system, but the company said flight bookings were not affected. The disclosure sent shares lower in early trading; the company had not yet confirmed how many customers or what data were accessed.

articles.title: Shein warns recovery will take time as e-commerce fees bite
articles.summary: Shein warned its European sales may not recover until the second half of 2027 after third-quarter European revenue fell 27.6% to $2.98 billion and group revenue declined 6% to $10.27 billion. New EU parcel charges and the end of duty-free import treatment have raised costs. The company cut marketing spending while investing in European warehouses and seeking faster growth in Latin America.

articles.title: South Korea unveils draft stablecoin rules, potential easing of ICO ban
articles.summary: South Korea’s financial regulator released draft rules that would let domestic banks issue stablecoins, digital tokens pegged to assets such as national currencies. The proposal could also reopen debate over the country’s nine-year ban on initial coin offerings. The legislation still needs parliamentary approval, and regulators are considering how fintech firms could participate. The scope, safeguards and implementation timetable remain unsettled.

articles.title: Retailers face rising AI cyberattack threat ahead of Black Friday, many uninsured
articles.summary: Retailers face heightened cyber risk heading into Black Friday as AI tools make attacks faster, Reuters reported. Insurer CFC’s data show ransomware claims against retail, leisure and hospitality businesses are 50% more frequent in November than the monthly average, while only 43% of small and midsize retailers carry cyber insurance. Seasonal sales, payment data and complex supply chains increase the potential cost of outages.

articles.title: Kremlin rejects ex-UK PM Johnson's call for a token Western force in Ukraine as unacceptable
articles.summary: The Kremlin rejected former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson’s proposal for even a small Western force in Ukraine, calling any foreign deployment unacceptable. Johnson argued a limited logistical presence far from the front would signal that Kyiv can choose its partners. Moscow has repeatedly warned such troops would be legitimate targets, while former president Dmitry Medvedev raised the risk of a Russia-NATO confrontation.

articles.title: Aramco, S-Oil inaugurate $7 billion petrochemicals complex in South Korea
articles.summary: Saudi Aramco and South Korea’s S-Oil inaugurated the $7 billion Shaheen petrochemical complex in Ulsan, Aramco’s largest investment in South Korea. The facility is expected to add about 3.2 million metric tons of annual petrochemical capacity, with commercial operations scheduled for 2027. It will use Aramco’s crude-to-chemicals technology and supply feedstock to nearby manufacturers, including industries serving electric-vehicle and semiconductor demand.

articles.title: New Miss Universe's Puerto Rican hometown celebrates her historic win
articles.summary: Puerto Rican contestant Jennifer Barreto, 27, won Miss Universe 2026, becoming the pageant’s first married mother to take the title. Her hometown of San Sebastián celebrated with public viewing parties and a caravan after the final. Barreto is Puerto Rico’s sixth winner, ending a 20-year wait for the island. The pageant began allowing married women and mothers to compete in 2023.

articles.title: Ukrainian drones attacked industrial facilities in Russia's Syzran, authorities say
articles.summary: Ukrainian drones struck industrial facilities in Russia’s Samara region, including the city of Syzran, while a separate strike killed one person in Samara, local authorities said. The region hosts major oil refineries, but Reuters could not verify social-media claims that two refineries were hit. Officials reported 145 drones downed and power outages; President Vladimir Putin had pledged retaliation for recent Ukrainian strikes.

articles.title: South Korea to unveil EV industry support measures as Chinese competition grows
articles.summary: South Korea plans to announce measures to strengthen its electric-vehicle industry as domestic automakers face growing competition from Chinese brands. The Finance Ministry told Reuters that a tax credit for EVs produced and sold in South Korea is under discussion, but no decision has been made. The government said the package would be presented Friday; Chinese-made vehicles accounted for 43.5% of new passenger EV registrations in the first nine months of 2026.

articles.title: Moldova keeps emergency energy measures in place despite opposition
articles.summary: Moldova’s pro-European government kept most emergency energy powers in place for another 30 days after a state of emergency expired. Officials said the measures helped stabilize gas, oil and electricity supplies, while water conditions had improved. Opposition parties demanded an accounting and criticized the policy. Moldova imports most of its energy and remains exposed to supply risks linked to regional tensions and Russia’s war in Ukraine.

articles.title: Deere forecasts 2027 profit below estimates as farm equipment recovery remains muted
articles.summary: Deere forecast fiscal 2027 net income of $4.50 billion to $5.25 billion, below analysts’ average estimate of $5.91 billion, as weak crop prices and high input costs restrain farm equipment purchases. The company reported quarterly revenue above expectations and said large-agriculture demand may be stabilizing in North America. It expects precision-agriculture sales to grow, while construction equipment benefits partly from AI data-center investment.

articles.title: US airlines face higher costs from proposed Embraer duty
articles.summary: A proposed 10% U.S. duty on finished Embraer aircraft from Brazil could raise costs for American airlines because there is no domestic alternative for the company’s regional jetliners, analysts and executives told Reuters. The tariff could begin as early as January, while carriers already face higher jet-fuel costs. The scope remains uncertain for aircraft completed in Florida from unfinished imports.

articles.title: Baseball's MLB sues players' union, seeks ruling that lockout is legal
articles.summary: Major League Baseball sued its players' union seeking a court declaration that an expected lockout beginning next week is legal, escalating talks over a new collective bargaining agreement. The central dispute is a proposed salary cap; MLB's latest offer would set a $258.2 million cap and $180.2 million floor in 2028. The union called the lawsuit frivolous and accused owners of avoiding good-faith bargaining.

articles.title: Mexico announces diplomatic protest after US denies extradition of former TV host
articles.summary: Mexico said it will send a diplomatic note protesting the United States' decision to deport former television host Inés Gómez Mont to Spain rather than extradite her to Mexico, where she faces allegations of tax fraud, money laundering and organized crime. President Claudia Sheinbaum cited reciprocity after Mexico transferred more than 90 suspects to U.S. custody. Spain has also received an extradition request; the allegations have not been adjudicated.

articles.title: UN tribunal says agency lacked evidence to dismiss Palestinian aid worker
articles.summary: A UN dispute tribunal ruled that UNRWA failed to provide evidence supporting its dismissal of Palestinian aid worker Abu Awad after Israeli allegations linked him to Hamas. It awarded him one year's pay and $5,000 in moral damages, while saying it could not determine the underlying allegations. The ruling raises questions about the agency's dismissal process; it does not resolve wider claims concerning other staff.

articles.title: Italian church report records 57 priests jailed for child sexual abuse
articles.summary: A report commissioned by the Italian Bishops' Conference documented 378 cases involving 356 alleged abusers and 385 victims between 2001 and 2021; 57 priests received final prison sentences. The authors cautioned that church archives cannot show the full scale of abuse. Victims' advocates called the figures incomplete and urged structural reforms and mandatory reporting, while the conference agreed to create a permanent observatory.

articles.title: Nigeria seizes $227 million of methamphetamine and arrests five Mexicans
articles.summary: Nigeria's anti-drug agency said it seized methamphetamine valued at $227 million in Enugu state and arrested five Mexican nationals. Officials said the operation recovered 1.5 metric tons of meth, 6.7 tons of precursor chemicals and industrial equipment. Authorities described it as one of the agency's largest hauls this year, amid concerns that Nigeria is becoming both a transit route and a production base for synthetic drugs.

articles.title: Ecuador says talks with US focused on reviewing joint security operations
articles.summary: Ecuador's interior minister said talks with U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth focused on reviewing joint operations, setting next steps and identifying Ecuador's needs. His comments followed a report that Washington paused joint military activity while investigating a deadly operation by Ecuadorean forces. The minister called the discussions productive and said an action plan remains in place; the status of any pause was not independently clarified.

articles.title: Nigeria's Tinubu vows to bring peace to insurgency-hit region
articles.summary: President Bola Tinubu promised to restore security in Nigeria's insurgency-hit northeast as he campaigns for a second term in the January 16 election. Borno state remains a Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province stronghold, while kidnappings and attacks continue. A recent poll cited by Reuters found more than half of respondents disapproved of his performance; Tinubu also said more than 70 abducted schoolchildren remained captive.

articles.title: Second US judge blocks Trump's latest birthright citizenship order
articles.summary: A federal judge in Washington blocked President Donald Trump's August order narrowing birthright citizenship, ruling that Supreme Court precedent left no room for the new exceptions. The injunction covers children in the class action and bars several federal agencies from enforcing the order against them. A second judge has now blocked the policy; the administration called the ruling activist and may appeal.

articles.title: Russian forces hit Kyiv with ballistic missiles, mayor says
articles.summary: Russian forces struck two sites in Kyiv with ballistic missiles late Wednesday, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. Two buildings on the east side of the Dnipro River were hit, with one badly damaged; casualties were possible, but officials had not confirmed a toll in the initial report. The attack adds to pressure on the capital as Russia continues missile and drone strikes across Ukraine.

articles.title: North Korea's Kim calls for wider deployment of tactical nuclear weapons
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspected facilities producing nuclear materials and conducting weapons research, state media reported, and called for wider deployment of tactical nuclear weapons across multiple domains. KCNA said Kim described production capacity as expanding and the country's nuclear status as non-negotiable. The report offers no independent details on the facilities or the scale and timing of any deployment.

articles.title: Islamic State attack kills two Syrian security personnel in Hasaka
articles.summary: An Islamic State attack on a security headquarters in Hasaka, northeastern Syria, killed two internal security personnel and wounded five, Syrian state media reported. Authorities said four attackers died, two in clashes and two in suicide explosions. Islamic State has continued operating through clandestine cells despite losing its last Syrian territory in 2019, and has renewed attacks on security forces under President Ahmed al-Sharaa.

articles.title: Senegal parliament opposes president's decision to implement revised budget
articles.summary: Senegal's National Assembly voted 128–9 to condemn President Bassirou Diomaye Faye's decision to implement a revised 2026 budget by decree after lawmakers rejected it. The dispute with former prime minister Ousmane Sonko's party threatens a proposed $2.2 billion IMF support programme tied to debt restructuring. Lawmakers said the government had not provided adequate transparency on public finances; Faye said he was safeguarding state operations.

articles.title: Barrick International chief meets Mali prime minister after mining dispute
articles.summary: Barrick Mining's newly appointed international-division chief met Mali's prime minister for the first time since the company and the military-led government settled a dispute over the Loulo-Gounkoto gold complex a year ago. The meeting suggests warmer relations after conflict over taxes, profit-sharing and control, during which four local executives were imprisoned. Barrick said it would comply with Mali's new mining code; it did not immediately comment.

articles.title: OPEC blames EU for COP31 collapse as fossil-fuel dispute deepens
articles.summary: OPEC Secretary-General Haitham Al Ghais rejected claims that oil producers caused the collapse of COP31, saying the EU and others walked away from negotiations. Producers opposed language on moving away from fossil fuels and backed carbon-capture references, which some developing nations called costly and unproven. Reuters also reported negotiators' concerns about Saudi influence; EU officials had not responded to OPEC's criticism.

articles.title: Fuel tanker crash ignites a massive fire on a highway surrounding Cairo, killing at least 31 people
articles.summary: A fuel-tanker crash on Cairo's Ring Road ignited a fire that killed at least 31 people and injured 21, Egypt's Health Ministry said. The blaze in Giza's Warraq district charred more than two dozen vehicles; prosecutors ordered DNA testing to identify victims. Officials said the toll was preliminary, renewing scrutiny of road safety and enforcement.

articles.title: US FinCEN takes some systems offline after cyber incident, official says
articles.summary: FinCEN took some systems offline after unauthorized access affected a limited subset of its network, a Treasury official told Reuters. Treasury is working with the FBI, CISA and outside forensic examiners to determine the scope. Officials said there was no evidence that Bank Secrecy Act or beneficial-ownership databases were breached; reporting relief was provided to filers disrupted by the outage. The investigation remains ongoing.

articles.title: US famine monitor to halt reporting as funding shortfall hits staff, sources say
articles.summary: More than half of FEWS NET's field staff could receive termination notices by December 1, leaving the U.S.-funded hunger-monitoring network unable to publish its planned December food-security update, Reuters reported. The State Department had not confirmed fiscal-year funding. FEWS NET works in more than 30 countries, including famine-risk areas such as Sudan, Yemen, South Sudan and Somalia; the timing of any funding restart remains unclear.

articles.title: FCC says SpaceX can deploy 1 million satellites for data centers in space. Scientists are skeptical
articles.summary: The FCC authorized SpaceX to deploy up to one million Starmind satellites for orbital AI data centers, requiring at least one station by 2033 and gradual expansion through 2040. Scientists questioned the plan's feasibility, citing heat removal in vacuum, launch and reentry pollution, orbital collisions, debris and interference with astronomy. The license does not guarantee the constellation will be built.

articles.title: Fed policymakers at odds over causes of high inflation
articles.summary: Federal Reserve officials remain divided over whether stubborn inflation reflects temporary supply shocks or stronger demand, Reuters reported ahead of the December policy meeting. Economists expected October headline PCE inflation of 3.8% and core inflation of 3.2%, while some policymakers warned AI investment and resilient spending could entrench price pressures. Markets were pricing in further rate increases, though falling oil prices complicate the outlook.

articles.title: Carthage resident Al Gore buys his hometown Tennessee newspaper
articles.summary: Former Vice President Al Gore agreed to buy the Carthage Courier, a 113-year-old weekly serving his Tennessee hometown and Smith County. The sale from the Lake family is expected to close in coming weeks; the price was not disclosed and all four employees are expected to remain. Gore, a former military and newspaper reporter, said he wants to preserve the paper as an independent local voice amid widespread newspaper closures.

articles.title: Lawsuits allege ICE brutalized U.S. citizens and prisoners at for-profit jail
articles.summary: Two people arrested during immigration raids in the Chicago area filed lawsuits alleging excessive force by federal agents; one plaintiff is a U.S. citizen who says agents rammed her car and restrained her after she identified herself. Separately, four former detainees allege sexual abuse, forced labor and retaliation at a Louisiana ICE facility. These are allegations in pending legal actions, not court findings.

articles.title: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia fuels Washington fight over China's chip access
articles.summary: Reuters reported that companies linked to Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive suspected by U.S. officials of ties to China's Ministry of State Security, financed up to 764 AI servers and modules valued at $270 million. The reporting also traced overseas data-center access and nearly 900,000 Nvidia and AMD chips approved for Chinese firms. Jensen Huang's reinstatement has intensified congressional efforts to tighten export controls; the alleged intelligence links remain unproven.

articles.title: Israeli judges recommend prosecutors drop one bribery case against Netanyahu
articles.summary: Judges in Benjamin Netanyahu's corruption trial recommended dropping one bribery case and reconsidering another, saying a conviction in the main case appeared unlikely. The recommendation is not a ruling; Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara said prosecutors would review the court's comments. Netanyahu denies wrongdoing. The cases concern alleged regulatory favors for favorable media coverage and a proposed deal with a newspaper publisher.

articles.title: Kenyan cult leader serving 200-year murder sentence convicted of new charges
articles.summary: Kenyan preacher Paul Mackenzie, already serving a 200-year sentence over the Shakahola starvation deaths, was convicted of five counts of child cruelty and one assault charge. A magistrate said he instructed followers to make children fast first; Mackenzie had pleaded not guilty and will be sentenced later. He was acquitted on other counts and still faces separate terrorism and manslaughter proceedings.

articles.title: Former Nazi guest house 'Eagle's Nest' being renovated after blaze
articles.summary: Workers are repairing Bavaria's Eagle's Nest, the former Nazi guest house, after an October fire destroyed its roof and remaining original furniture. A man suspected of starting the blaze is being held in a psychiatric facility while the investigation continues. The site once drew about 300,000 visitors annually. Critics say it should remain in ruins to deter neo-Nazi pilgrimages; operators argue preservation supports monitored remembrance.

articles.title: UN peacekeepers evacuate Ebola response workers trapped by fighting in eastern Congo
articles.summary: U.N. peacekeepers evacuated 10 health workers from a hospital in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo after fighting between government forces and an armed group disrupted the Ebola response. The clashes in Ituri province also displaced civilians, while other workers sheltered in a maternity ward. The mission said it was unclear whether anyone remained trapped. Reuters reported the outbreak had caused 11,955 cases and 5,867 deaths.

articles.title: Israeli opposition advances October 7 attack probe opposed by Netanyahu
articles.summary: Israel's opposition-led parliament gave initial approval to a bill creating an independent commission to investigate security failures before Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack. The measure passed 65–50 but needs three more votes. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu opposes an independent inquiry and favors a government-shaped process. The vote comes as rival Gadi Eisenkot tries to assemble a coalition after Netanyahu's bloc lost its majority.

articles.title: Suspected militants kill at least 30 in Nigeria's Niger state, residents say
articles.summary: Residents told Reuters that suspected militants killed at least 30 people and burned homes in villages in Nigeria's Niger state, describing the assault as retaliation for earlier killings of Fulani herders. A village head said gunmen occupied some communities and blocked recovery of bodies; Reuters could not independently verify a circulating video. The governor announced compensation for victims' families and urged dialogue.

articles.title: "I'm going to drive": FAA outage and high fares reshape Thanksgiving travel plans
articles.summary: Thanksgiving travel is being reshaped by a Nov. 13 FAA communications outage that disrupted more than 18,000 flights and affected about one million passengers, alongside domestic airfares averaging $469, up 57% year over year. Airlines forecast nearly 29 million passengers Nov. 20–30, down from 31 million last year; some travelers are driving or taking buses and trains instead.

articles.title: Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers says he found out about benching from teammate
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers said he learned of his benching from teammates, not coach Mike McCarthy, and accused the coach of falling asleep in meetings and missing team events. AP reported McCarthy and the Steelers did not directly address the accusations; Rodgers was excused from practice, and Mason Rudolph is set to start against Denver. The claims are Rodgers's account; the team has not publicly confirmed them.

articles.title: Federal Reserve survey finds modest growth but persistent price pressures
articles.summary: The Fed's latest Beige Book found slight-to-moderate growth in eight districts and no change in four, while consumer spending was flat and firms reported persistent energy, transport, health-care, insurance and tariff costs. AI-related data-center investment remained strong. The report adds business-level context ahead of the December meeting; October PCE inflation was 3.8% year over year, with core inflation at 3.3%, Reuters reported.

articles.title: Two men in court accused of stealing cufflinks from Prince William's house
articles.summary: Two men appeared in a Norwich court accused of breaking into Anmer Hall, the Prince and Princess of Wales's Norfolk residence, and stealing six pairs of cufflinks and a clock. Prosecutors said they climbed a drainpipe to reach a dressing room; a third suspect remains at large. The defendants were remanded in custody and did not enter pleas. Kensington Palace said it would not comment on security matters.

articles.title: Iraq's top court backs federal troop deployment and Baghdad control of Kurdistan borders
articles.summary: Iraq's Federal Supreme Court ruled that Baghdad may deploy federal forces along all international borders, including crossings in the semi-autonomous Kurdistan region, and oversee border agencies and oil fields. The decision backs Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's effort to centralize security and resource control after ordering federal forces to take over Kurdish-run crossings. Kurdish authorities rejected what they called military threats and urged talks.

articles.title: Army detonates lead azide in Iowa despite toxic plume fears
articles.summary: The Army said its controlled detonation destroyed all five tons of degraded lead azide without secondary explosions or infrastructure damage. EPA monitors detected no airborne lead one hour later; the agency had collected more than 1,200 baseline air, soil and water samples and deployed more than 300 staff and contractors. Follow-up monitoring continues, so initial readings are not a final environmental assessment.

articles.title: Drone strikes kill 19 civilians in Sudan's Blue Nile state, rights group says
articles.summary: Emergency Lawyers said drone strikes in Damazin, Blue Nile state, killed 19 civilians, including six women. The group blamed the Rapid Support Forces; AP reported 15 wounded, while an earlier Reuters account cited 20, leaving the injury count unsettled. The attacks add pressure on a region receiving displaced families as Sudan's war continues.

articles.title: New York bans AI chatbot toys for five years over child-safety concerns
articles.summary: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul signed a five-year prohibition on making, distributing or selling children’s toys that use internet-connected AI companion chatbots. The law takes effect Feb. 22, 2027, and violations can bring civil penalties of up to $15,000 per day. Officials cite risks involving inappropriate conversations, emotional manipulation and children’s privacy; the ban does not cover this holiday shopping season.

articles.title: Seven-year-old held at Texas immigration center asks Trump to release her
articles.summary: Seven-year-old Charlotte Ortiz, held with her mother at the Dilley family immigration center in Texas, wrote President Donald Trump asking to return to school and see her father. Her 29 days in detention exceed a 20-day limit established by a 1985 court settlement. DHS says her mother has a final removal order; the family disputes the circumstances. The case adds scrutiny to family detention and conditions at Dilley.

articles.title: Yemen's army reports 654 operations against Houthi positions
articles.summary: Yemen’s internationally recognized army said government forces carried out 654 operations against Houthi positions, killing or wounding 109 fighters and commanders. The military described 21 airstrikes, 577 artillery attacks, 36 drone strikes and 20 rocket-artillery strikes across several fronts, but provided no independent evidence; the Houthis had not commented. The claims come amid renewed fighting and a worsening humanitarian crisis after the 2022 truce collapsed.

articles.title: Nearly 800 displaced from Sudan's Abu Zabad in one day, IOM says
articles.summary: The International Organization for Migration said at least 795 people fled Sudan’s Abu Zabad area in West Kordofan in one day as fighting between the army and Rapid Support Forces intensified. Displaced families moved into neighboring localities and states, following several larger waves earlier in November. The agency described conditions as tense and volatile; the conflict, which began in 2023, has displaced about 13 million people.

articles.title: German police in North Rhine-Westphalia to replace Palantir with Celonis
articles.summary: Police in Germany’s North Rhine-Westphalia state plan to replace Palantir’s data-analysis software with a system from Munich-based Celonis after a Europe-wide tender. The new program will run on police-owned infrastructure, giving authorities greater control over data and processes; the contract may last seven years. Palantir criticized the decision, while privacy officials have raised concerns about sensitive data access by US intelligence services.

articles.title: Gordon Ramsay to lead BBC's Top Gear revival planned for 2028
articles.summary: The BBC named celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay as the lead presenter for Top Gear’s planned return in 2028, with co-hosts still to be announced. Filming is expected to begin in 2027. The motoring show has been off air since a 2022 crash seriously injured former presenter Andrew Flintoff. The revival follows a pause announced in 2023 after the accident, which halted production.

articles.title: Netanyahu's Likud challenges results at 120 Israeli polling stations
articles.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party filed a court appeal seeking new voting at 120 Israeli polling stations, citing alleged irregularities involving voter-identification information, according to Israeli media. The reports said the filing did not allege widespread fraud or bribery. Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party accused Likud of trying to delegitimize the result. Eisenkot faces a Dec. 6 deadline to form a government.

articles.title: Austria's population projected to peak in mid-2040s before decline
articles.summary: Statistics Austria projects the country’s population will peak at 9.36 million in the mid-2040s before declining to 9.04 million by 2080, revising earlier forecasts that suggested it could exceed 10 million. Fertility is expected to fall to 1.3 births per woman, while the share of residents aged 65 and older may reach 30.1% by 2080. Immigration and employment patterns will shape the pace of aging.

articles.title: Poland plans no-fly zone along eastern border to bolster NATO flank
articles.summary: Poland plans a restricted airspace zone along its eastern border, potentially taking effect in late December or early January, Deputy Defense Minister Cezary Tomczyk said. The zone would extend several to dozens of kilometers inland as Warsaw strengthens NATO’s eastern flank after Russian missiles fell in eastern Poland. Tomczyk said any decision to intercept threats over Ukraine would require agreement among NATO members.

articles.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine awaits US date for next round of peace talks
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv is waiting for Washington to schedule another round of US-mediated talks with Russia, which he wants to include European representatives. Previous discussions in Abu Dhabi produced agreement in principle to broaden participation, but Russian officials said no decision had been made. The next meeting’s timing and format remain uncertain as strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure continue.

articles.title: Malaysia studies AI wealth fund to distribute technology gains
articles.summary: Malaysia is studying an artificial-intelligence wealth fund that could distribute some economic gains to citizens, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said. He directed the communications and digital ministries to examine options, citing a proposal by US Senator Bernie Sanders. Anwar also said foreign AI investors face conditions on water infrastructure and skills training, reflecting concern that rapid automation and investment could widen inequality and disrupt jobs.

articles.title: Israeli strike in Gaza kills Hamas security official, wife and children
articles.summary: An Israeli strike on Gaza City's Shati refugee camp killed Hamas northern Gaza internal-security chief Mohammad Majid Abu al-Ouf, his wife and two teenage daughters, according to Gaza officials. AP reported four deaths and six wounded; Israel's military confirmed it targeted al-Ouf. The attack came amid a series of strikes reported during an already fragile ceasefire.

articles.title: ‘It’s been really a mess’: Meta insiders concerned over push to AI content moderation
articles.summary: Meta employees told the Guardian that the company’s accelerated shift from human moderators to AI systems has left smaller review teams and increased the scale of mistaken removals. Staff described difficulties handling nuance and languages beyond English, while researchers documented a rise in account takedowns. Meta denied political bias and said newer systems make fewer errors on average; the company’s opaque moderation process makes independent assessment difficult.

articles.title: 'Russia wants more than Ukraine,' says Germany's Merz as he defends aid for Kyiv
articles.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz defended continued military aid to Ukraine and a planned rise in German defence spending, saying Russia’s ambitions extend beyond Ukraine and its actions threaten wider European security. He cited tensions around the Baltic, Poland and cyber infrastructure; Moscow denies seeking confrontation with NATO. The position faces domestic opposition as cost-of-living pressures grow, while Germany plans to lift defence spending above €200 billion by 2030.

articles.title: 53 incoming House Democrats plan to boycott Harvard orientation over graduate-worker strike
articles.summary: Fifty-three newly elected House Democrats told Harvard they will skip a December orientation program if graduate student workers remain on strike. The lawmakers said attending would mean crossing a picket line. The dispute centers on wages and workplace protections, with the graduate union seeking higher raises than Harvard has offered. The boycott adds political pressure to negotiations but does not directly resolve the labor dispute.

articles.title: A new way to measure tides could improve local flood forecasts
articles.summary: Researchers at the Technical University of Munich and Oxford used four decades of satellite shoreline images to estimate tidal height along beaches at 100-metre intervals. They found differences approaching one metre across New Zealand's South Taranaki Bight, finer variation than conventional gauges and broad satellite averages reveal. The method could improve local flood and storm-surge forecasts, especially where tide gauges are sparse, though it needs wider testing.

articles.title: African insurgents take war to the skies with off-the-shelf drones
articles.summary: Reuters documents how inexpensive first-person-view drones are reshaping conflicts across Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger. Armed groups have used tactics refined in Ukraine to threaten military vehicles, aircraft and infrastructure, eroding governments’ former air advantage. The reporting also describes Ukrainian training links to Sahel separatists. The shift raises security risks for regional forces and facilities, though the balance of power varies by country.

articles.title: Norse Atlantic suspension forces Pakistan's PIA to shift UK flights to its own fleet
articles.summary: Pakistan International Airlines said it will move UK routes to its own Boeing 777 fleet from Nov. 26 after Norse Atlantic abruptly suspended wet-lease operations, cancelling two flights as passengers prepared to board. The disruption follows Norse’s warning that its finances were critical and its shares had plunged 76%. The carrier’s funding needs and ability to resume operations remain uncertain.

articles.title: All hostages rescued after Colombian supermarket siege ends
articles.summary: Colombian security forces stormed a supermarket in Cartagena after a 17-hour siege that began with an attempted armoured-vehicle robbery. President Abelardo de la Espriella said all hostages were rescued and one captor was killed; about 30 people were initially held, with 10 released during negotiations. Authorities described the hostages as safe, but the motive and full circumstances of the attempted robbery remain under investigation.

articles.title: Amazon to launch Amazon Autos in UK in early 2027 in first expansion beyond US
articles.summary: Amazon says it will expand its car marketplace to the United Kingdom in early 2027, its first move beyond the United States. Hyundai will be an initial partner, listing new and used electric, hybrid and petrol models; dealer group Vertu will also participate. Customers will browse, compare prices and reserve vehicles online, but complete purchases at dealerships, which retain control over pricing.

articles.title: Amnesty urges war-crimes probe into Ethiopian shelling in Tigray
articles.summary: Amnesty International urged an independent investigation after verifying 14 civilian deaths in four Ethiopian artillery attacks on Alamata in September. It also alleged that Tigrayan forces placed fighters in residential areas and schools, claims the TPLF rejected; Ethiopian authorities had not responded. The report comes amid renewed clashes and military movements near the Eritrean border, raising fears that the fragile 2022 peace agreement could unravel.

articles.title: AP photo essay documents homelessness beneath Barcelona's prosperous landmarks
articles.summary: An Associated Press photo essay documents people sleeping rough beneath Barcelona’s grand civic and commercial buildings as Spain’s housing crisis becomes a central election issue. A local nonprofit estimated about 2,000 people slept on the city’s streets nightly in December 2025, 43% more than in 2023. New-lease rents rose 42% over a decade, while shelters face waiting lists and complex referral rules.

articles.title: AP review: Disney's animated film 'Hexed' offers a familiar coming-of-age witch story
articles.summary: Disney's animated film 'Hexed' follows a teenager who discovers magical powers and enters a hidden witch realm, where her grandmother rules as queen. The Associated Press review praises the voice performances of Hailee Steinfeld, Jodie Foster and Rashida Jones, along with the film's visuals, but finds the chosen-one plot familiar and its middle section slow. The review sees the mother-daughter relationship as the film's strongest element.

articles.title: Atlantic hurricane season ends unusually quiet under strong El Niño
articles.summary: The 2026 Atlantic hurricane season is effectively over with 10 named storms and only one hurricane, Isaias, the quietest season since 1983 by accumulated cyclone energy, according to the Washington Post’s meteorological analysis. A strong El Niño helped suppress Atlantic storms while supporting unusually active Pacific conditions. Forecasters say next year’s outlook remains uncertain because ocean temperatures and the El Niño–La Niña transition could change.

articles.title: Australia and Solomon Islands sign security treaty barring foreign military bases
articles.summary: Australia and Solomon Islands signed a security treaty naming Australia the island nation's primary security partner and barring foreign military or security bases on Solomon Islands territory. The pact follows concern over a 2022 agreement with China; Prime Minister Matthew Wale would not confirm reports that the Chinese deal will not be renewed in 2027. Australia also pledged cooperation on infrastructure, education, renewable energy and sport, while Beijing said its Pacific partnerships are not driven by rivalry.

articles.title: Australia passes broad new online safety law targeting harmful platform content
articles.summary: Australia passed a Digital Duty of Care law requiring online platforms to take proactive steps against harmful content and features, with potential fines of up to 5% of global revenue. The rules take effect in a year and permit regulators to use anonymous accounts during investigations. Technology groups warn the law’s broad definitions could encourage excessive removals and raise privacy concerns.

articles.title: Australia's Labor government wins Greens support for trust and private-jet tax changes
articles.summary: Australia's Labor government secured Greens support for changes to discretionary trusts after agreeing to end a tax concession for private-jet fuel and exempt pensioners from proposed cuts to older Australians' private-health rebates. A minimum 30% tax rate on trust income is projected to raise A$4.5 billion in its first year from 2029–30. The agreement helps move several bills through the Senate, but opposition figures say the tax changes could burden small businesses.

articles.title: Australian inflation heats up in October, core hits two-year high
articles.summary: Australia’s monthly consumer-price index rose 0.5% in October, taking annual inflation to 4.9% from 4.3%, Reuters reports. Fuel costs jumped 6.3%, while trimmed-mean inflation reached 3.8%, its fastest pace since 2024. The figures are above the Reserve Bank’s 2%–3% target band and have reduced market confidence in near-term rate cuts, although weak labor-market conditions still shape expectations.

articles.title: Bangladesh minimum wage hike misses garment worker demands, sparks fresh protests
articles.summary: Bangladesh approved a 36% increase in the garment-sector minimum wage, lifting monthly pay to about $138, but the raise fell short of workers’ demands and triggered fresh clashes with police near Dhaka. The industry employs more than four million people and generates over 80% of export earnings. Reuters reports weeks of protests disrupted production and prompted some buyers to shift orders abroad.

articles.title: Berlin landlord warns expropriation proposals could deter property investment
articles.summary: Commercial property group Aroundtown warned that Berlin proposals to expropriate landlords with more than 10,000 apartments could discourage investment beyond the city. The debate has returned after state elections strengthened the Left Party, which backs taking over large housing portfolios. Aroundtown says uncertainty may reduce financing and property transactions, while arguing Germany's housing shortage requires more construction. The company says converting some office space to homes could help add supply.

articles.title: BP transfers 3,000 finance operations employees to India's Wipro
articles.summary: BP has agreed to transfer 3,000 finance operations employees in India, Hungary and Malaysia to Indian technology-services company Wipro during 2027, subject to conditions. The deal reflects a broader shift by multinational companies to outsource internal support functions as they seek lower costs and more automation. BP will retain oversight of standards and data, while Wipro gains experienced staff and a long-term service relationship.

articles.title: Bulgaria intercepts migrant boat carrying 35 people, including children
articles.summary: Bulgarian authorities intercepted a boat carrying 35 migrants after it entered the country's Black Sea waters and came ashore near Sinemorets. Children were among those taken for medical care and warm clothing, regional officials told state news agency BTA. Bulgaria recorded about 7,000 attempted entries by land and sea in the first nine months of 2026, down from roughly 12,270 during the same period in 2025.

articles.title: Cambodia and China begin largest Golden Dragon joint military exercise
articles.summary: Cambodia and China began their eighth Golden Dragon joint military exercise, described by Cambodian officials as the largest since the drills started in 2016. The 15-day program includes counterterrorism, anti-piracy, humanitarian assistance and disaster relief. The cooperation underscores Beijing’s close relationship with Phnom Penh and draws attention to the Chinese-funded expansion of Cambodia’s Ream Naval Base, which Cambodia says is open to friendly navies.

articles.title: Cardamom advertisement sparks legal dispute between Bollywood actor and Indian regulator
articles.summary: Bollywood actor Ajay Devgn is challenging a Maharashtra food-safety order telling him to stop appearing in advertisements for a cardamom product linked to a brand also known for banned betel-nut mixtures. Regulators say such promotions can act as indirect advertising for restricted products; Devgn argues cardamom itself is legal. The court case could help define India's rules on surrogate advertising, an issue with implications for public-health policy and celebrity endorsements.

articles.title: Catalan separatist Carles Puigdemont says he will return to Spain in December
articles.summary: Former Catalan leader Carles Puigdemont says he will end nearly a decade in Belgium and return to Spain on December 12, after the Supreme Court applied a 2024 amnesty law to close his criminal case. He plans to present a renewed independence proposal five days later. His return could affect post-election coalition talks, although support for Catalan secession has weakened as voters focus more on immigration, crime and housing.

articles.title: CD Projekt RED says GTA VI launch has not materially hurt fourth-quarter business
articles.summary: Polish game maker CD Projekt RED says the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI has not materially hurt its fourth-quarter business, despite a dip in console engagement. Its chief executive noted that GTA VI had not launched on PC, where many of the company’s players are based. Third-quarter net profit fell 43%, leaving a demanding fourth-quarter target for its multi-year profit goal.

articles.title: China investigates Shanghai party chief in widening anti-graft campaign
articles.summary: China’s anti-corruption watchdog opened an investigation into Shanghai party chief Chen Jining, a member of the ruling Communist Party’s Politburo. Reuters says he is the fourth Politburo member targeted since 2025, following removals involving senior military and provincial officials. Authorities gave no details about Chen’s case; the probe nevertheless signals that Xi Jinping’s campaign continues to reach the party’s highest ranks.

articles.title: China misusing Interpol to target dissidents, says leading UK lawyer
articles.summary: A British lawyer who handles Interpol red-notice cases says China is using the system to pursue dissidents through criminal allegations that may conceal political motives. He cited five cases and raised questions about notices sought against UK-based Chinese activists ahead of Hong Kong hosting Interpol’s general assembly. Interpol said it was reviewing his inquiry but shared no substantive information. The claims are allegations; China and Interpol had been approached for comment.

articles.title: China urges Netherlands to provide certainty for firms amid Nexperia dispute
articles.summary: China's foreign minister urged the Netherlands to provide a predictable business climate for Chinese companies during talks with Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen. The appeal comes amid a continuing legal dispute over Nexperia, the Dutch-based chipmaker owned by China's Wingtech, after Dutch authorities intervened over national-security concerns. Both governments said they would keep communication open on semiconductors, but the company's control and governance remain contested.

articles.title: China-linked battery projects could receive UK funding despite security warnings
articles.summary: Ofgem's provisional shortlist for a UK long-duration storage subsidy scheme includes 11 lithium-ion projects, many reliant on batteries and software from Chinese suppliers. The Guardian reports that security specialists and industry sources worry the regulator's cost-focused assessment may underweight cyber risks over facilities' lifetimes. Ofgem says it is reviewing consultation responses; final funding decisions are expected in coming weeks. The debate pits cheaper storage against supply-chain resilience and domestic technology.

articles.title: China's Shenzhou-24 docks at space station with Pakistani national as first foreign astronaut
articles.summary: China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft docked with Tiangong on Nov. 25, carrying Pakistani pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who became the first Pakistani in orbit and is set to be the station’s first foreign visitor. Ali will work as a payload specialist for five to 10 days, while a Chinese astronaut remains for a year to study long-duration spaceflight. The mission highlights expanding China-Pakistan space cooperation.

articles.title: Citigroup weighs return to Venezuela after five-year absence
articles.summary: Citigroup is considering restoring banking services in Venezuela, five years after leaving the country, Bloomberg reported. Reuters says executives have discussed possible arrangements and sanctions waivers with U.S. State and Treasury officials; a first step could be correspondent banking rather than branches. Citi declined to comment. Any return would face a country still recovering from prolonged economic crisis and financial isolation.

articles.title: Cognizant in talks to take over parts of S&P Global's Capital IQ operations
articles.summary: Cognizant is in talks to take over parts of S&P Global’s Capital IQ operations, potentially transferring about 1,500 employees in India, Reuters reports, citing two people familiar with the discussions. The terms remain unsettled and talks could fail. The move comes as S&P explores strategic options for its data businesses and companies increasingly outsource operations to reduce costs and reshape units for AI-era services.

articles.title: Container of Christmas decorations washes ashore in Bulgaria
articles.summary: Bulgarian authorities opened a shipping container that washed ashore near Burgas and found more than 80 boxes of Christmas decorations, including life-sized Santa figures and a polar bear. The cargo, valued at about €50,000, reportedly belongs to a Romanian company and may have come from a Greek vessel hit by drones in the Black Sea last month. The ship operator has not confirmed the container’s origin.

articles.title: Democrats clinch historic House majority of at least 259 seats
articles.summary: Democrat Victoria Broderick’s narrow Tennessee victory gave House Democrats at least 259 seats, their largest majority since 1992. AP said she defeated Republican Scott DesJarlais by fewer than 400 votes, a 0.18-point margin. One House race remained too close to call, while two Louisiana contests were headed to December runoffs. The result expands Democrats’ leverage when the new Congress convenes in January.

articles.title: Dolphins with active social lives and big friendship groups live longer, researchers find
articles.summary: A study in PLOS Biology used nearly 40 years of observations from Shark Bay, Western Australia, to link stronger, more stable social groups with longer lives among Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins. Researchers say group ties can help animals share information, find mates and maintain alliances, while also carrying risks such as disease transmission and stress. The findings show individual social preferences change with age; they do not establish that social contact alone causes longevity.

articles.title: EasyJet annual profit plunges 89% as fuel costs surge
articles.summary: EasyJet reported full-year pretax profit of £71 million, down 89% from the previous year, as fuel costs rose 11% to £2.5 billion despite a strong summer travel season. Reuters says the result missed analyst expectations and comes as Apollo’s £5.7 billion takeover proceeds toward a planned 2027 completion. The airline withheld next-year guidance because of the pending deal.

articles.title: English coastal communities receive £11 million for erosion planning and monitoring
articles.summary: Britain will distribute more than £11 million across 12 council-led projects to help English coastal communities monitor erosion and plan for rising seas. Measures include laser-equipped drone surveys, dune restoration, 3D modelling and moving roads inland. The Environment Agency estimates 3,500 properties could be at risk by 2055 and over 10,000 by 2105. The funding is intended to support earlier planning; it cannot prevent all shoreline retreat or protect every property.

articles.title: EU postpones discussion to approve Tesla's self-driving tech
articles.summary: The European Union postponed a committee meeting that could consider bloc-wide approval of Tesla’s assisted-driving system from December 1 to December 15. A vote may occur then, but approval would require support from 15 member states representing 65% of the EU population. The delay follows two earlier meetings without a vote after the Netherlands granted preliminary approval in April.

articles.title: Europe plans €50 billion sovereign tech equity fund to boost quantum technology
articles.summary: The European Commission proposed a Quantum Act with a targeted €50 billion equity fund to help European companies scale quantum computing, secure communications and sensing technologies. The draft would favor EU suppliers in some public procurement while allowing bids from certain partner countries. EU governments and the European Parliament must still negotiate the law. The proposal aims to narrow a funding gap with the United States and China.

articles.title: Eurostar cancels trains linking London, Paris and Brussels after staff strike
articles.summary: Eurostar cancelled at least six services linking Brussels, Paris and London after staff began an unannounced strike, the company said. The operator did not specify how long the stoppage would last or provide further details to Reuters. The cancellations add uncertainty for cross-Channel travellers during a busy holiday period; passengers should check directly with Eurostar because the scale and duration of disruption were still unclear at publication.

articles.title: Ex-England soccer player Sterling spared immediate jail sentence for dangerous driving
articles.summary: Former England winger Raheem Sterling received a 12-month prison sentence suspended for 18 months after admitting dangerous driving while inhaling nitrous oxide before crashing his Lamborghini. A court also ordered 100 hours of unpaid work and a two-year driving ban. No one was injured. The judge cited the danger to other road users, while noting Sterling had engaged with addiction services after the incident.

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE: Boehly signs US-backed share swap deal to buy Lukoil global assets
articles.summary: Todd Boehly said he signed an agreement for a consortium including the U.S. International Development Finance Corp. to acquire sanctioned Russian oil company Lukoil’s overseas energy assets. The proposed swap values the portfolio at about $16 billion in assets for $10 billion in securities; U.S. Treasury approval is still required. The operations span 11 countries, and Washington would receive a stake and share of future profits.

articles.title: Federal judge permanently blocks sanctions against groups that share ICC evidence
articles.summary: A federal judge made permanent an injunction blocking the Trump administration from penalizing two organizations for sharing evidence with the International Criminal Court and Palestinian rights groups. The groups challenged an executive order threatening civil fines and criminal penalties for such cooperation. The court ruled that the order imposed an unconstitutional, content-based restriction on speech, limiting enforcement against the plaintiffs.

articles.title: Flood at unauthorized Indonesian gold mine leaves nine dead and 17 missing
articles.summary: Floodwaters killed at least nine miners at an unauthorized gold mine in West Java, while rescuers searched for 17 people believed trapped underground. Heavy rain caused the nearby Ciseureuh River to overflow into a roughly 100-metre shaft. Authorities said the illegal operation delayed notification by about 16 hours; 325 rescuers were working in difficult conditions. The disaster highlights hazards in Indonesia’s informal mining sector.

articles.title: German economy grows just 0.1% in third quarter after downward revision
articles.summary: Germany’s economy expanded just 0.1% in the third quarter of 2026, below an earlier 0.2% estimate, the federal statistics office said. Reuters attributes the revision to weaker exports and September retail activity. Investment fell 1.2% from the prior quarter, while household consumption rose only 0.1%, reinforcing signs that growth slowed after stronger first-half performance.

articles.title: Glee actor Jenna Ushkowitz says Cory Monteith tribute episode came too soon
articles.summary: Jenna Ushkowitz, who played Tina on 'Glee,' says the 2013 episode honoring co-star Cory Monteith aired too soon after his death. She told Variety that cast and crew were grieving privately while also acting out their characters' grief, and felt they lacked the support to handle both. Ushkowitz understood why fans wanted a tribute, but said the experience was painful. Monteith died in 2013 from an accidental overdose.

articles.title: Global airports court private capital to fund upgrades, raising cost concerns
articles.summary: Airport operators are turning again to private investors to help fund aging terminals, control towers and capacity expansions. Reuters says industry estimates point to more than $4 trillion in global airport infrastructure needs over three decades as passenger traffic could double by 2050. Officials warn private financing can raise costs, leaving governments to balance capital needs against user fees and affordability.

articles.title: Global temperatures stayed more than 2°C above preindustrial levels for six straight days
articles.summary: Global daily temperatures exceeded 2°C above preindustrial levels for six consecutive days for the first time, reaching 2.24°C above baseline on Monday, according to data reviewed by The Guardian. Scientists stress that a short daily streak does not mean the Paris Agreement's long-term threshold has been breached. They link the spike to human-caused warming and a strong El Niño, warning that drought and forest fires can amplify carbon buildup.

articles.title: Gold falls 3% to more than one-year low after data shows US inflation rose further
articles.summary: Gold fell more than 3% on November 25, with spot bullion near $3,446 an ounce, its lowest level since August 2025. Investors reacted to stronger U.S. inflation data and expectations of a Federal Reserve rate increase in December. Higher interest rates make non-yielding gold less attractive, while fresh tariff and geopolitical risks add uncertainty to the outlook.

articles.title: GSK reports twice-yearly asthma drug matched Nucala in late-stage immune-disorder study
articles.summary: GSK said its twice-yearly medicine depemokimab performed comparably to its monthly drug Nucala in a late-stage study for the rare immune disorder EGPA. The company reported similar safety and efficacy, but detailed results have not yet been published. GSK plans to seek regulatory approval in the first half of 2027; the findings do not yet make the drug an approved EGPA treatment.

articles.title: Gulf stock markets mixed as traders assess Saudi tensions and US inflation
articles.summary: Gulf stock markets were mixed as investors assessed Saudi-Houthi escalation and awaited U.S. inflation data that could influence Federal Reserve policy. Saudi Arabia’s benchmark slipped 0.3%, while Dubai and Abu Dhabi edged higher; Qatar fell. Saudi Arabia also approved a 2027 budget projecting a 190-billion-riyal deficit. The figures are an early trading snapshot, not a full-day market result.

articles.title: Hollywood stars defend Iranian director Jafar Panahi after Tehran court sentences him in absentia
articles.summary: Nearly 2,000 actors, directors, festivals and film institutions had signed a statement backing Iranian filmmaker Jafar Panahi, according to Democracy Now. Panahi was sentenced in absentia by a Tehran court to five years and one month in prison. The Cannes Film Festival issued a separate protest, urging authorities to lift restrictions that prevent him from traveling, creating and expressing himself freely.

articles.title: Homeland Security secretary faces White House criticism over outage response
articles.summary: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin faces criticism inside the White House over his handling of major technology outages and public appearances during the disruption. Officials say he was removed from television briefings after struggling to explain flight, banking and corporate-system failures. President Trump publicly backed him, while lawmakers seek answers about the outages and the department’s broader management and immigration enforcement.

articles.title: Hong Kong wildlife groups seek tighter exotic-pet rules after millions of imports
articles.summary: Conservation groups say Hong Kong imported 3.7 million live exotic animals from 86 countries and jurisdictions between 2020 and 2025, roughly 80 each hour. They are urging authorities to create an approved-species list and update rules that currently exclude some amphibians and invertebrates. Researchers warn poorly regulated trade can spread pathogens and parasites to people and native wildlife. Hong Kong's agriculture department had not responded to Reuters by publication.

articles.title: Houthis say they attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery
articles.summary: Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, Riyadh's financial district and the ports of Jeddah and Jizan. Saudi-led forces said they intercepted four drones aimed at the refinery, while Reuters cited imagery and a source indicating a hit. Brent crude rose 3.5% to $94.61 and WTI gained 2% to $83.68; the full damage remains disputed.

articles.title: In landmine-ravaged Myanmar, a rebel with an artificial leg vows to fight on
articles.summary: Myanmar recorded 1,891 landmine and unexploded-ordnance casualties in 2025, the highest national toll for a third straight year, according to Landmine Monitor. Reuters followed a rebel commander who lost a lower leg and received a prosthetic near the Thai border, where a small workshop has fitted 150 people wounded in the conflict. Mines laid by both military and resistance forces contaminate nearly two-thirds of the country, putting civilians at continuing risk.

articles.title: India approves $1.2 billion incentive plan for construction equipment
articles.summary: India approved an eight-year, $1.2 billion incentive programme to expand domestic production of advanced construction equipment and reduce reliance on imports, particularly from China. The plan offers sales-linked support to manufacturers and component suppliers, plus grants for testing. It gained urgency after Chinese export controls on tunnel-boring machines took effect November 18. Officials estimate the programme could attract $2.27 billion in investment and replace some imports.

articles.title: India's central bank buys dollars for a fourth straight month
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India was a net buyer of foreign currency for a fourth consecutive month in September, purchasing $6.94 billion net, according to its monthly bulletin. Gross purchases reached $82.18 billion and sales $75.25 billion. The bank's forward dollar sales also increased. The data reflect efforts to manage currency flows, although the rupee later strengthened in November as oil prices eased and investors shifted toward Indian equities.

articles.title: Iran says it can withstand US naval blockade as inflation pressures mount
articles.summary: Iran’s first vice president said Tehran can withstand the U.S. naval blockade because more cargo is entering through land borders, while the government seeks to contain basic-goods prices. October consumer prices were 88.7% higher than a year earlier and food and beverage prices rose 112.6%, according to Iran’s statistics agency. Officials offered no quantified supply assurances, leaving the effect of the blockade uncertain.

articles.title: Iran says ships hit mines in Hormuz, warns vessels to coordinate passage
articles.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers struck mines and caught fire while using what Tehran called an unauthorized route through the Strait of Hormuz. AP separately reported the IRGC's claim that an LPG tanker was hit after disabling its tracking system. The vessels were not independently identified, and the claims remain unverified; Iran warned ships to coordinate passage with its forces.

articles.title: Japan's key services inflation gauge hits 36-year high
articles.summary: Japan’s services producer-price index rose 4.2% year over year in October, the fastest pace since 1990, according to Bank of Japan data cited by Reuters. Higher ocean freight, leasing and hotel costs drove the increase. The measure helps show whether companies are passing labor expenses to customers, strengthening the case for a possible near-term central-bank rate increase.

articles.title: Vance says Jensen Huang won't need a pardon as scrutiny of Nvidia scandal builds in Washington
articles.summary: Vice President JD Vance said Jensen Huang is not under investigation and does not need a pardon, while Trump had called a pardon an option. Huang is scheduled for closed-door House interviews Dec. 1 and a public Senate hearing Dec. 3. S&P separately placed Nvidia on negative credit watch over unresolved board oversight and governance risks.

articles.title: Jordan court sentences man to death over attack that killed security officer
articles.summary: Jordan’s State Security Court sentenced a man to death for an attack that killed a security officer near the Sri Lankan Embassy in Amman on November 5. The court convicted him of terrorist acts resulting in death and weapons offenses, according to the armed forces. The ruling remains subject to appeal and automatic review, so it is not yet a final sentence.

articles.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia arrives in Spain after departure deal with US
articles.summary: Salvadoran migrant Kilmar Abrego Garcia arrived in Spain after leaving the United States under an agreement with US authorities, ending a legal fight that reached the Supreme Court. He was wrongly deported to El Salvador in 2025 despite a court order, then returned to the US after the justices intervened. His lawyer calls the move temporary and says future legal avenues could allow him to return as a permanent resident.

articles.title: Kiwi return to Wellington hills after 150 years in Māori-led conservation milestone
articles.summary: A Māori-led conservation partnership has returned more than 250 wild kiwi to the hills around Wellington, where the birds had been absent for over 150 years. The Capital Kiwi project used more than 5,300 predator traps across 24,000 hectares to reduce stoat threats; its founder estimates the local population now exceeds 300, including wild-hatched chicks. Project leaders report chick survival above 90% in managed areas, though long-term success depends on sustained predator control.

articles.title: Labour remains committed to ban on conversion practices despite calls to scrap bill
articles.summary: Britain’s Labour government says it remains committed to a proposed ban on conversion practices in England and Wales, despite calls to amend or abandon the bill over free-speech, parenting and religious-freedom concerns.
