Equalities minister Bridget Phillipson said the measure targets abuse intended to change sexual orientation or gender identity and would not affect normal parenting. Details remain contested as the draft is debated.

articles.title: Latest review of Met police culture finds little has changed since last one
articles.summary: An independent review found institutional racism, misogyny and homophobia remain in London’s Metropolitan Police three years after the Casey report. It cited defensive leadership, weak organisational learning and staff fear of retaliation: only 44% felt confident raising concerns about a senior officer, while 17% had no confidence. The Met points to misconduct and vetting reforms, but the review warned further scandals remain likely without deeper cultural change.

articles.title: Lebanon prepares to reopen a second international airport in its north
articles.summary: Lebanon plans to reopen Kleiat Airport in the north as an international gateway from mid-December, with initial routes expected to serve Turkey, Egypt and Jordan. Private investors are expected to contribute up to $6 million, while the government upgrades roads. The project could bring jobs and travel links to the impoverished Akkar region. Its progress also reflects Hezbollah's reduced political influence after recent wars and shifts in Lebanon's power balance.

articles.title: Italy rebukes Ukraine over attacks on Russian ships in Libya
articles.summary: Two Libyan naval officers died from wounds suffered in Ukraine's drone strike on a Russian warship docked at Benghazi, the eastern Libyan National Army said. Ukraine said it deployed seven sea drones; President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the vessel as a military target. Italy's foreign minister rebuked Kyiv, warning the operation violated Libyan sovereignty and risked widening the conflict.

articles.title: London Metal Exchange tightens aluminium trading rules after supply squeeze
articles.summary: The London Metal Exchange temporarily tightened short-term aluminium trading rules after falling inventories and concentrated holdings drove immediate-delivery premiums to their highest level since 1988. The changes require large holders of stock warrants and short-term futures to make metal available at capped prices. Available exchange inventories have more than halved this year. The LME says it will keep monitoring the market and may take further action if the squeeze persists.

articles.title: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed until Saturday because of storm
articles.summary: Macy's moved its 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade from Thursday to Saturday at 8:30 a.m. Eastern after forecasts of a major storm raised safety concerns for participants, spectators and the large balloons. New York City officials confirmed the decision, which marks the first weather-related postponement in the parade's history. The event had previously been suspended only during World War II.

articles.title: Major fragrance suppliers fined £85 million by the CMA for illegal collusion
articles.summary: The UK Competition and Markets Authority fined Firmenich, Givaudan and International Flavors & Fragrances a combined £85 million after finding they shared sensitive information on pricing and commercial negotiations. The regulator said some firms coordinated price increases and agreed not to hire staff assigned to a major customer. The companies admitted breaking competition law; the fragrances are used in household cleaners, detergents, perfumes and colognes.

articles.title: Malawi hospitals face worst essential-medicine shortages in more than a decade
articles.summary: Essential-medicine availability in Malawi has fallen from 77% in early 2025 to 40% nationwide and as low as 18% at major referral hospitals, according to internal government supply data. Patients are being asked to buy basic items privately, even in public hospitals. The crisis is tied to foreign-exchange shortages and about $18 million in supplier arrears; officials say they have begun clearing debts to restore deliveries.

articles.title: Meta executives meet India's opposition amid protests over content moderation
articles.summary: Meta executives met India’s opposition Congress party as protests intensified over content removals and allegations that the company favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s BJP, which Meta denies. Reuters reported Meta restricted more than 5.4 million posts or accounts under Indian law in the first half of 2026, up from about 70,000 in all of 2025. The company made no commitments at the meeting and cited local legal requirements.

articles.title: Migrant arrivals in Spain's Canary Islands break single-day record
articles.summary: More than 2,100 migrants arrived in Spain's Canary Islands in a 24-hour period, a new single-day record, according to maritime rescue data. One person was found dead and another gave birth during the crossing from West Africa. Most boats reached El Hierro, a key entry point. The arrivals intensified pressure on Spain's migration debate ahead of an election, while officials called for stronger regional cooperation and legal routes.

articles.title: Millions of UK households face 26% energy price-cap increase in January
articles.summary: Britain’s Ofgem raised the household energy price cap by 26% for January–March, taking the annualized bill for a typical dual-fuel household to £2,166. Reuters says the increase will affect about 20 million homes on variable tariffs and reflects higher wholesale gas prices linked to the Middle East conflict. The jump is likely to add pressure to household budgets and inflation.

articles.title: More than 490,000 Russian soldiers have died during Ukraine war, leaked data suggests
articles.summary: Leaked Russian government records analyzed by BBC News and Mediazona suggest at least 490,334 Russian soldiers had died since the full-scale invasion began in 2022; another analysis of the dataset puts the toll closer to 700,000. The records reportedly contain more than 11 million entries through September 2026. The Kremlin has not released official totals and says only its Defense Ministry can publish them.

articles.title: Nationwide Greek strike disrupts ferries, metro and some flights
articles.summary: Greek public-sector workers and several private unions staged a nationwide strike demanding higher wages, restored annual bonuses and stronger health and education services. Ferry routes stopped, some metro services were cut and flights at regional airports were suspended as transport and telecommunications workers joined the action. The strike is the third in recent weeks amid pressure from rents and living costs; the government points to €2.2 billion in tax breaks and aid this year.

articles.title: Native American group wins partial ruling over Plymouth's National Day of Mourning protest
articles.summary: A Massachusetts judge ruled that Plymouth must honor a 1998 agreement allowing the United American Indians of New England to hold its National Day of Mourning protest without permits or insurance. The town no longer has to provide a mobile stage, however, and the ruling leaves room for future legal disputes. The group says the event will proceed, challenging efforts it views as limiting Indigenous speech and visibility.

articles.title: Netherlands pushes back against proposed US chip-export control bill
articles.summary: The Netherlands is lobbying against the proposed U.S. MATCH Act, which would pressure allies including the Netherlands and Japan to tighten export controls on chipmaking equipment sold to China or face unilateral U.S. restrictions. Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen said Dutch export-control decisions should remain independent. ASML expects China to account for about one-fifth of its 2026 sales, making the dispute commercially significant.

articles.title: Nine more Ukrainian children reunited with families through US-backed effort
articles.summary: Nine Ukrainian children have been reunited with relatives, bringing the total to 43 under an initiative involving US first lady Melania Trump, the White House and Russian officials. The children were moved from Russia and Russian-held parts of Ukraine to relatives in Ukraine and Germany. Moscow says cooperation was secured with both sides, while Ukrainian authorities had not immediately commented. The cases remain sensitive amid international allegations about the wartime transfer of children.

articles.title: North Korea expels Swiss diplomatic office head in sanctions dispute
articles.summary: North Korea ordered Swiss diplomatic representative Sylvain Astier to leave within 48 hours, saying Switzerland's sanctions against the Songdowon International Children's Camp were hostile. The move came less than a month after Bern reopened its Pyongyang liaison office. Switzerland says the office is intended to preserve dialogue despite disagreements; analysts see the expulsion as a warning that Pyongyang may reject diplomatic engagement while sanctions remain in place.

articles.title: North Korea orders Swiss diplomat out and demands closure of Pyongyang office
articles.summary: North Korea ordered the head of Switzerland's newly reopened diplomatic office to leave within 48 hours and demanded the office close, calling Swiss sanctions on a children's camp hostile. Switzerland says the camp was involved in transferring Ukrainian children from Russian-occupied areas and promoting pro-Russia messaging. Pyongyang rejects the sanctions and says the camp is legitimate. Switzerland says it will keep diplomatic channels open despite the dispute.

articles.title: Oat sales rise as shoppers seek filling foods amid GLP-1 popularity
articles.summary: Waitrose says sales of its Scottish oats rose 124% this year as shoppers seek filling, fibre-rich foods amid the popularity of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs. A retailer survey found 64% of respondents were actively choosing foods that help them feel full for longer, while many GLP-1 users reported changing household shopping. The Guardian notes that social-media labels such as 'nature's Ozempic' are marketing shorthand: oats are not equivalent to prescription medication.

articles.title: Paralympian Ezra Frech becomes first Paralympian to win Dancing with the Stars
articles.summary: Paralympic track-and-field gold medalist Ezra Frech won the U.S. edition of Dancing with the Stars, becoming the show's first Paralympian champion and youngest male winner. The 21-year-old and professional partner Daniella Karagach beat Olympic figure skater Amber Glenn and four other finalists. Their freestyle included a prosthetic-leg mishap, but Frech recovered and finished the routine; judges' scores and viewer votes determined the result.

articles.title: Peppermint oil linked to lower blood pressure in small 20-day trial
articles.summary: A randomized study of 40 adults with elevated blood pressure or stage 1 hypertension found that participants taking food-grade peppermint oil had an average systolic reduction of about 8.5 mmHg versus placebo after 20 days. The University of Lancashire team published the findings in PLOS One. The trial was small and brief, so larger studies are needed; it does not justify replacing prescribed treatment.

articles.title: Plane crash off the coast of Mississippi kills 6, including 2 children
articles.summary: A Cessna 210 traveling from New Orleans to Fort Myers crashed in the Gulf of Mexico between Pascagoula and Horn Island, killing all six aboard, including two boys ages 8 and 10, the Coast Guard said. Divers recovered the victims from the fuselage after a lengthy search. The FAA and National Transportation Safety Board will investigate; officials have not announced a cause.

articles.title: Pope creates Vatican initiative to coordinate Catholic prison ministry
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV created a Vatican service to coordinate Catholic pastoral care for prisoners worldwide, naming Buenos Aires Archbishop Jorge Ignacio García Cuerva as its first coordinator. The office will help local churches organize prison visits, train volunteers and liaise with civil authorities. The move formalizes a priority Leo inherited from Pope Francis and follows Leo’s recent visits to prisons in Equatorial Guinea and Argentina.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV urges major changes after UN climate talks end without agreement
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV expressed concern after UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, ended without an overarching agreement, with negotiators divided over whether to address fossil fuels. He said climate-related disasters are increasingly frequent and called for changes in behavior, economic systems and governance. The appeal echoes Pope Francis's environmental focus but does not settle the disputes that blocked consensus at the summit.

articles.title: Poundland collapses into administration, putting 12,000 jobs at risk
articles.summary: Poundland’s directors appointed AlixPartners as administrators after rescue bids failed, putting about 12,000 jobs across 600 UK and Irish stores at risk before Christmas. Stores and distribution centres will remain open while administrators explore a sale of the business or its assets. The retailer has struggled with inflation, competition and funding shortages; the outcome for individual sites and staff remains uncertain.

articles.title: Private capital investment in emerging markets jumps 19% on China tech and infrastructure
articles.summary: Private-capital investment in emerging markets rose 19% through the third quarter to $143.2 billion, the Global Private Capital Association said, driven by Chinese technology funding and infrastructure demand. The total is already close to all of 2025's $158.3 billion. China attracted $64.3 billion, while infrastructure investment also increased in Africa and Central and Eastern Europe. The figures cover reported investment through September, not a full-year forecast.

articles.title: Proposed 2030 census changes could remove race question and add citizenship question
articles.summary: The Census Bureau is considering removing its race-and-ethnicity question and adding a citizenship question to the 2030 census, proposals that civil-rights groups and researchers say could distort population data. Census information guides representation, funding, public-health research and infrastructure planning. Advocates warn a citizenship question could discourage responses in immigrant communities; officials argue alternative data sources exist. The proposals have drawn criticism after the public-comment period closed.

articles.title: Pulitzer-winning composer Caroline Shaw reflects on a career across classical and pop music
articles.summary: Composer, singer and violinist Caroline Shaw discusses a career spanning Pulitzer-winning contemporary music, classical ensembles and collaborations with pop artists including Phoebe Bridgers and Rosalía. The Guardian profile follows her work with the Attacca Quartet and upcoming Barbican residency, while Shaw reflects on the importance of respect, curiosity and enjoying performance rather than treating every project as a relentless cycle. Her schedule remains unusually broad across classical, theatre and pop.

articles.title: Real Madrid beats PSV 5–1 as Arsenal and Manchester City draw in Champions League
articles.summary: Real Madrid recovered from a halftime deficit to beat PSV Eindhoven 5–1, with Jude Bellingham scoring a standout goal, and kept a perfect Champions League record. Arsenal drew 1–1 with Borussia Dortmund after conceding an equaliser, while Manchester City twice fell behind before drawing 2–2 with Napoli. The results left Madrid top of the league-phase standings, with Arsenal and City dropping points in the fifth matchday.

articles.title: Rory Culkin discusses anxiety, fatherhood and the pressure of acting
articles.summary: In a Guardian interview, actor Rory Culkin discusses anxiety that affected auditions and performances, his decision to stop pushing himself through punishing preparation, and the support he received from his mother and siblings. He also talks about fatherhood and his attraction to darker roles, including his new crime-drama work. The profile offers his own account of a difficult period in his career rather than a broader assessment of Hollywood or mental health.

articles.title: Russia extradites Chinese national wanted over alleged $2.25 billion deposit scheme
articles.summary: Russia has extradited a Chinese national, identified only by the surname Shu, to China, where he is wanted over an alleged scheme involving more than 15 billion yuan ($2.25 billion) in public deposits. Xinhua, citing China’s Ministry of Public Security, said he returned on November 5. Authorities disclosed few details about the alleged fundraising or the extradition process.

articles.title: Russian government official warns of Ukrainian drone attacks on utility infrastructure this winter
articles.summary: Russia’s deputy prime minister said preparing for possible Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian power and heating infrastructure is a top winter priority, especially in border regions. Reuters reported that some facilities near Moscow have anti-drone netting and residents are buying generators and batteries. Last year, attacks near Belgorod left tens of thousands without heat and electricity; Kyiv and Moscow continue to trade strikes on energy sites.

articles.title: Russian strikes target Ukraine's power transmission network, leaving Odesa households without electricity
articles.summary: Russia has increasingly targeted substations and transmission lines that move electricity between Ukrainian regions, rather than only attacking power stations, DTEK's Odesa grid chief told Reuters. He said 60% of regional substations had been struck, some repeatedly. Repairs restored much of the supply, but about 9,000 households remained without power after another overnight attack. Odesa lacks local generation, making its links to western Ukraine especially important.

articles.title: Saudi national kidnapped by suspected Islamic State militants in Niger, sources say
articles.summary: Two security sources told Reuters that suspected Islamic State militants kidnapped a Saudi national in Niger on November 21 or 22 and are holding the person hostage. One source placed the abduction in western Tillaberi, near Mali and Burkina Faso; the other gave a location between Tillaberi and Niamey. No group has claimed responsibility, and Nigerien and Saudi authorities did not respond to requests for comment.

articles.title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court bid to overturn Farmgate panel report
articles.summary: South Africa’s High Court set aside a panel report that said President Cyril Ramaphosa may have breached the constitution in connection with the “Farmgate” scandal. Reuters’ brief report did not detail the court’s reasoning or the practical effect beyond overturning the report. The ruling changes the legal status of the panel’s findings, but it does not by itself resolve every allegation surrounding the affair.

articles.title: Spain and Morocco compete to host the 2030 World Cup final
articles.summary: Spain and Morocco are competing to host the 2030 World Cup final, with Spain’s Bernabéu and Camp Nou facing Morocco’s planned 115,000-seat Hassan II stadium near Casablanca. The contest is complicated by rivalry between Madrid and Barcelona, political tensions and FIFA leadership issues. FIFA has not announced the venue, and inspections of host cities are still underway.

articles.title: Spain election puts housing policy at center of contest over rent caps and construction
articles.summary: Spain’s November 29 election has turned on housing, with conservative leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo promoting Madrid-style deregulation and Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez defending Catalonia’s rent caps and limits on short-term lets. Both sides promise more construction, but economists disagree about how supply reforms and rent controls affect prices. The vote could determine which approach becomes national policy.

articles.title: Spain’s climate crisis receives little attention in election debate
articles.summary: Spain’s election debate has given limited attention to climate policy despite recent wildfires and floods, The Guardian reports from a community still recovering from summer fire damage. Experts say voters often rank immediate economic and housing concerns above climate risks, while politicians avoid an issue that can polarize constituencies. The gap raises questions about preparedness and compensation as extreme weather continues to affect the country.

articles.title: Spain's Indra targets rapid defence and space growth through 2035
articles.summary: Spanish defence and technology group Indra set revenue targets above €12 billion by 2030 and €20 billion by 2035, relying on rising European military spending. Its €22 billion order backlog provides visibility, and defence revenue is projected to quadruple to €5.2 billion by 2030. The company also expects space revenue to exceed €1 billion, although its new plan sets a lower 2030 core-profit margin than its previous strategy.

articles.title: SpongeBob SquarePants cast reflects on 27 years as new holiday special arrives
articles.summary: The cast and creators of 'SpongeBob SquarePants' are marking more than 27 years since the series began, ahead of a new holiday special. The animated show remains a major television and merchandise franchise, with more than $17 billion in retail sales and 353 billion minutes watched on YouTube, according to figures cited by AP. Creators credit its mix of humor and family appeal for sustaining multiple generations of fans.

articles.title: Study links GLP-1-associated weight loss with higher breast density and mammogram callbacks
articles.summary: A study of 107 women taking GLP-1 drugs for at least a year found breast density increased after an average 40-pound weight loss, with a 22.4% mammogram recall rate compared with roughly 10% nationally. Four biopsies were benign. Researchers say the change may reflect loss of breast fat rather than more breast tissue; they advise continuing routine screening and telling imaging teams about GLP-1 use and substantial weight loss.

articles.title: Sydney fire-ant colony with multiple queens prompts expanded eradication response
articles.summary: New South Wales officials expanded their response after a red imported fire-ant nest found in Sydney's Auburn suburb proved larger and more complex than first thought. The colony has multiple queens, a form that can support denser nests and is harder to eradicate. Authorities say it is the second Sydney detection this year and are tracing possible supply-chain routes; residents are urged to report sightings rather than disturb nests.

articles.title: Taiwan comedian keeps performing under security after alleged attack plot
articles.summary: Taiwanese comedian Huang Yi-hao continues performing with security present after prosecutors charged five people over an alleged plot to injure him following jokes about China’s leader. Reuters reports Huang was slightly injured when struck by a car in September; investigators allege a Chinese national paid a local man to attack him. Beijing has rejected Taiwan’s accusations of involvement, and the case has become a flashpoint over speech and intimidation.

articles.title: Tata Steel's complex APL Apollo deal draws investor backlash
articles.summary: Tata Steel's proposed combination with Indian steel-tube maker APL Apollo could create a business with 7.5 million metric tons of annual capacity, but the deal structure has angered investors. Tata plans to sell its finished-products unit, buy a major stake from APL Apollo's chair and make a further open offer. A separate manufacturing agreement for the chair's private firm has raised governance concerns, while both companies' shares fell sharply.

articles.title: These young Republicans have a message for their party: It’s time to ‘grow up’
articles.summary: Several dozen young Republicans in Tarrant County, Texas, met after the party’s midterm losses to discuss its direction. Many criticized personal attacks, infighting and limited progress on affordability, while urging stronger leadership and a return to conservative principles. Others favored a harder line. The discussion offers a local snapshot of tensions over Trump’s influence as Republicans look toward 2028.

articles.title: Taiwan says it is confident of keeping previously agreed tariffs with US
articles.summary: President Donald Trump proposed new maximum tariffs of 20%–40% on 14 trading partners, citing excess industrial capacity. Taiwan said it expects its previously agreed 15% U.S. rate to remain, pointing to earlier trade and investment arrangements covering semiconductors and other exports. The proposals remain subject to consultation, and the U.S. trade representative says existing negotiated caps may limit the final rates.

articles.title: U.S. new home sales jump to 10-month high as builders cut prices
articles.summary: U.S. new single-family home sales rose 14.2% in October to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 701,000, their highest level since December 2025, as builders cut prices to attract buyers. The median price fell 3.2% year over year to $391,300. Higher mortgage rates and elevated unsold inventory remain obstacles, and economists expect housing-market weakness to persist into 2027.

articles.title: U.S. third-quarter GDP growth revised sharply higher to 4.3%
articles.summary: U.S. third-quarter GDP was revised to a 4.3% annualized pace from 3.4%, the fastest in three years. Consumer spending was upgraded to 4.2% and business equipment investment grew 21.8%, much of it tied to AI. Higher-income households drove much of the spending and savings fell, leaving economists watching whether investment and consumption can sustain the pace.

articles.title: UK competition watchdog weighs remedies for proposed $25 billion AkzoNobel-Axalta merger
articles.summary: Britain's Competition and Markets Authority said proposed remedies from AkzoNobel and Axalta could address concerns over their planned $25 billion merger. AkzoNobel offered to sell its European and UK vehicle-refinishing coatings business to preserve competition. The CMA will consult on the proposal and a potential buyer before making a final decision; the regulator previously warned the combined company could hold 40% to 50% of the UK market.

articles.title: UK considers opening BBC iPlayer to advertising and rival broadcasters
articles.summary: Britain is advancing plans to let BBC iPlayer carry content from rival broadcasters and potentially advertising, according to people familiar with the discussions. The changes would require a technology overhaul costing tens of millions of pounds and could be outlined in a government paper on the BBC's charter renewal. The proposal aims to help public-service broadcasters compete with global streaming platforms, but would alter the service's current licence-fee-based model.

articles.title: UK embassy in Japan warns of rise in drink spiking and credit card fraud at Tokyo bars
articles.summary: Britain’s embassy in Tokyo warned visitors about drink-spiking and extortion at nightlife venues in districts including Shinjuku, Roppongi and Shibuya. Police recorded 340 cases in Shinjuku between January and October, 195 more than a year earlier; one alleged charge reached ¥9.6 million. Authorities say foreign tourists are frequent targets, while the true number may be higher because some victims discover fraud only after leaving Japan.

articles.title: UK nuclear test veterans win 40-year battle for inquiry into Cold War tests
articles.summary: Britain’s prime minister authorized an independent inquiry into the health effects of Cold War nuclear tests after a campaign lasting about 40 years. An estimated 22,000 British service members witnessed tests from 1952 to 1967; veterans say some were exposed to fallout without adequate protection. The panel will examine disputed records and claims, with an interim report expected by October 2027.

articles.title: UK reportedly moves military aircraft into hangars at night amid drone concerns
articles.summary: Britain's Royal Air Force is moving aircraft into hangars and shelters at night and considering anti-drone netting, according to reports by The Times and Sky News. The Ministry of Defence had not commented. The reports follow warnings from British security agencies about sabotage threats and suspected unauthorised drone activity near military bases, including incidents authorities have linked to possible Iranian involvement.

articles.title: UK watchdog says Colman's sale could ease concerns over $65 billion Unilever deal
articles.summary: Britain’s Competition and Markets Authority said a proposed sale of Unilever’s Colman’s brand could help resolve concerns about McCormick’s planned $65 billion acquisition of Unilever’s food business. The regulator will assess the proposal before deciding whether to clear the deal with conditions or open a deeper investigation. Colman’s makes mustard, sauces and recipe mixes central to the competition review.

articles.title: UK watchdog warns funding uncertainty threatens defence investment plan
articles.summary: Britain’s National Audit Office warned that uncertain funding and underestimated costs threaten delivery of the Defence Investment Plan. The Ministry of Defence has limited assurance it can complete the programme, while planned efficiency savings of nearly £11 billion by 2029–30 are only partly supported by detailed plans. The watchdog also cited reduced training spending and higher costs linked to the Iran war.

articles.title: Ukraine says strike on Russian air base damaged five military aircraft
articles.summary: Ukraine's General Staff said its forces struck Savasleyka air base in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region, damaging three MiG-31 jets and two Su-34 fighter-bombers used in attacks on Ukraine. Russia had not immediately commented, so the reported damage could not be independently confirmed. The strike is part of Kyiv's campaign against Russian military infrastructure as Moscow continues attacks on Ukrainian cities and energy facilities.

articles.title: Underemployment among young U.S. college graduates reaches six-year high
articles.summary: Underemployment among U.S. college graduates aged 22 to 27 reached 42.5% in September, the highest level since 2020, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. Many recent graduates are working in roles that do not require degrees or relying on part-time and contract work. Economists cite weak hiring, uncertainty and employers’ use of AI, while noting degrees still tend to improve long-term outcomes.

articles.title: US grocers serve up Thanksgiving deals even as turkey prices climb
articles.summary: Major U.S. retailers are offering Thanksgiving meal kits at or below last year's prices to attract inflation-weary shoppers, even as wholesale turkey and potato costs rise. Reuters reported frozen whole-turkey prices reached record highs, while grocers absorb some of the increase to signal value. Walmart's 26-item meal kit costs $35 for ten people, five dollars less than last year. Retailers hope shoppers add higher-margin extras.

articles.title: US inflation accelerates again in October as Fed rate-hike expectations grow
articles.summary: The US Personal Consumption Expenditures price index rose 0.3% in October and 3.8% over the year, while core inflation reached 3.3%, according to government data. Consumer spending also increased, supported largely by higher-income households. Financial markets are pricing in another Federal Reserve rate increase in December and possibly January. Persistent inflation is eroding wage gains and may slow household spending as 2027 approaches.

articles.title: US jobless claims fall to 189,000, pointing to a steady labour market
articles.summary: New US applications for unemployment benefits fell by 13,000 to 189,000 in the week ending November 21, below economists' expectations. Continuing claims also declined, suggesting layoffs remain limited even as hiring is subdued. The figures were released a day early because of Thanksgiving. A stable labour market could give the Federal Reserve more room to keep raising rates as it tries to bring inflation back toward its 2% target.

articles.title: US orders for core business equipment rise more than expected in October
articles.summary: Orders for US-made non-defence capital goods excluding aircraft rose 1.2% in October, beating economists' expectations and extending a run of strong business-equipment investment. Shipments also increased, supporting the equipment-spending component of GDP. AI infrastructure investment has helped drive recent growth, but investors are questioning the cost and returns of data-centre expansion. Durable-goods orders rose more modestly as weaker aircraft orders offset gains elsewhere.

articles.title: US-Mexico intelligence cooperation may ease tensions after cartel leader's capture
articles.summary: Mexico's arrest of Sinaloa-linked figure Fausto Isidro Meza Flores followed months of planning and U.S. intelligence support, including a surveillance drone deployed at Mexico's request. Analysts told AP the operation could offer a model for cooperation without U.S. troops operating on Mexican soil. Tensions remain over sovereignty and extradition: Washington seeks custody, while Mexico says he will face prosecution there first.

articles.title: US-sought activist Fergie Chambers says extradition case should not punish his political beliefs
articles.summary: James 'Fergie' Chambers, a U.S. citizen sought for extradition by Washington over allegations linked to support for Hamas and protest activity, told The Guardian he fears being targeted for his political views. A Spanish court released him on bail after identifying problems with translations in the U.S. request; proceedings are paused while the issue is reviewed. Chambers denies wrongdoing, and any extradition remains unresolved as he pursues asylum in Spain.

articles.title: Walmart-backed PhonePe restarts IPO plans at up to $15 billion valuation
articles.summary: Indian digital-payments company PhonePe has resumed preparations for an initial public offering and is targeting a $12 billion to $15 billion valuation in early 2027, a source told Reuters. The proposed sale could raise $1.2 billion to $1.5 billion, mainly allowing Walmart and other investors to reduce or exit holdings. PhonePe has more than 650 million registered users and processed nearly half of India's UPI transactions in October.

articles.title: Walmart-owned Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down
articles.summary: Walmart-owned Flipkart said chief executive Kalyan Krishnamurthy will leave after more than 11 years leading the Indian e-commerce group. The company says product and technology chief Balaji Thiagarajan will run the business temporarily while a successor is selected. Flipkart has more than 500 million registered users and has long prepared for a possible public listing, though no timetable was announced.

articles.title: With new league in planning stages, NBA announces $11B initiative for arena development in Europe
articles.summary: The NBA announced an initiative targeting at least €10 billion (nearly $11 billion) from global investors to build or modernize arenas and related entertainment districts across Europe. The financing is intended to support clubs in a planned NBA-FIBA league expected to begin next fall. Potential markets include Britain, France, Spain, Italy, Germany, Greece and Turkey, but no participating cities have been selected.

articles.title: Wolf comeback divides the densely populated Netherlands
articles.summary: Wolves, absent from the Netherlands for about two centuries, have returned in growing numbers, but their recovery has sparked conflict in the densely populated country. Researchers estimate fewer than 150 animals in about 15 packs, while farmers report thousands of livestock losses. The government says it plans to permit some culling to prevent attacks; conservationists argue coexistence measures remain essential.

articles.title: AI stock rout deepens but damage is limited by afternoon bounce
articles.summary: AI-linked shares plunged early Wednesday but recovered much of the loss by the close as investors weighed debt-heavy data-center expansion and uncertain returns. The Nasdaq Composite and Nasdaq-100 each ended down 0.6%, after the Nasdaq-100 briefly approached a 20% decline from its October record. Nvidia closed down 3.9%, SoftBank fell 14% in Tokyo, and CoreWeave's 2031 bond yield neared 18%.

articles.title: Yemenis prepare to flee as Houthis advance toward Aden
articles.summary: Residents and aid groups in Aden are preparing for possible evacuation as Houthi forces mass north and east of the city, roughly 50 miles away, and could cut key roads. The Houthis have not declared an immediate assault, but a siege or capture would sharply weaken Yemen’s Saudi-backed government. The advance compounds a humanitarian emergency: 18.7 million people face acute food insecurity and more than 350,000 have been displaced since August.

articles.title: CDC reports nine verified measles-related deaths in the U.S. in 2026 as tallies diverge
articles.summary: The CDC counted nine verified measles-related deaths in the United States in 2026 and 6,039 confirmed cases across 47 jurisdictions through Nov. 24. Public state reports, however, imply at least 14 associated deaths, exposing a gap between federal and state tallies after the CDC changed its verification method. The agency said 11% of patients were hospitalized, with the highest rate among children under five, and warned totals may change.

articles.title: India says U.S. deported 1,700 Indian nationals so far in 2026
articles.summary: India’s foreign ministry said the United States deported 1,700 Indian nationals between January and Nov. 25, below the 3,567 recorded in 2025 but up from 1,273 reported through July 2026. The ministry says it verifies each person’s nationality before accepting returns. It provided no monthly breakdown, and the figures exclude people merely identified for removal or still in immigration proceedings.

articles.title: Todoist says breach exposed email addresses and legacy password hashes for 6% of users
articles.summary: Todoist said an attacker used a stolen development credential to reach its cloud systems and download account data affecting about 6% of users, including email addresses, legacy password hashes and account-creation dates. A much smaller group had API or Slack tokens accessed, while limited task and Outlook content was searched for credentials. The company says it blocked access, revoked exposed tokens and protected affected accounts.

articles.title: Allstate outage leaves customers unable to access policies and claims before Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Allstate’s website and mobile app remained unavailable for multiple days before Thanksgiving, leaving customers unable to review policies, pay bills, submit claims or use app-based roadside assistance. TechCrunch reported the outage began Monday and affected customers nationwide. The insurer had not publicly explained the cause or provided a restoration timeline, forcing some customers to contact local agents by phone or email.

articles.title: Hera spacecraft reveals crater and boulders on asteroid struck by NASA
articles.summary: Europe’s Hera mission released the first close-up images of Dimorphos, the asteroid NASA’s DART spacecraft struck in 2022. The images show a stadium-sized flattened crater, chaotic tumbling and hundreds of orbiting boulders. DART shortened Dimorphos’s orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes; Hera’s follow-up measurements will help scientists understand how asteroid structure affects deflection and improve future planetary-defense planning.

articles.title: BNP Paribas moves into higher global systemic-bank category, raising capital buffer
articles.summary: BNP Paribas moved into a higher systemic-risk category on the Financial Stability Board’s 2026 list, raising its required extra capital buffer from 1.5% to 2%. MUFG moved down to a 1% buffer, while the list remained at 29 banks and JPMorgan stayed highest at 2.5%. The revised buffers take effect Jan. 1, 2028, affecting how much loss-absorbing capital major lenders must hold.

articles.title: Pacifica Pier partially collapses as king tides and powerful waves batter Bay Area coast
articles.summary: Pacifica's municipal pier partially collapsed into the ocean as exceptionally high king tides combined with waves larger than forecast, flooding streets and homes along Northern California's coast. The Chronicle reported two minor injuries after a wave struck three people at Stinson Beach; shelter-in-place orders were issued near Santa Cruz. Officials warned surf remained dangerous even after the peak tide passed.

articles.title: China extends suspension of ban on US-bound gallium, germanium, antimony exports
articles.summary: China extended until Jan. 27, 2027, its suspension of restrictions on U.S.-bound exports of gallium, germanium, antimony and certain superhard materials, while keeping tighter end-use reviews for graphite. The pause had been due to expire Nov. 27. The minerals feed semiconductors, fiber optics, batteries and defense supply chains; the extension gives Washington and Beijing more time to maintain a fragile trade truce.

articles.title: Yemen officials say strike on buses, trucks kills 26
articles.summary: An airstrike on a bus and trucks in Yemen’s Lahj province killed 26 people, including 14 civilians and 12 Houthi fighters, according to local officials cited by AFP. The Houthis blamed the Saudi-led coalition, while government forces said the Houthis carried out the attack. The conflicting accounts have not been independently resolved; the strike occurred near a front line advancing toward Aden.

articles.title: Sanofi's $41 billion Insmed bet charts life beyond Dupixent
articles.summary: Sanofi agreed to acquire U.S. respiratory-drug maker Insmed for $41 billion in cash, offering $175 a share, a 17.5% premium to the prior close. The deal would add marketed medicines and a respiratory pipeline as Sanofi seeks growth beyond Dupixent ahead of patent expiries in the early 2030s. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027, subject to approvals; analysts say it does not resolve every pipeline risk.

articles.title: Senegal reinstated as 2025 African champions, Morocco to contest decision
articles.summary: Senegal was reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champion after the Court of Arbitration for Sport unanimously overturned CAF’s decision to award Morocco a 3-0 forfeit. CAS restored Senegal’s 1-0 extra-time win, saying the referee’s choice to resume the final after the team’s walk-off was a field-of-play decision. Morocco said it would challenge the ruling; Senegal and the arbitrator denied alleged improper contact.

articles.title: Justice Department announces largest-ever crackdown on scammers, targeting over 800 defendants
articles.summary: The Justice Department said it had taken action in more than 400 cases involving over 800 defendants since a March executive order targeting scam networks. The department cited charges, extraditions, convictions and international raids; the FBI said Operation Blackout seized nearly $17 billion in illicit funds and prevented more than $690 million in potential losses. Those figures are the administration's reported enforcement results, not an independent estimate of recovered victim money.

articles.title: Nearly 7,000 killed or injured by landmines, war remnants in 2025, highest toll in 5 years
articles.summary: The Landmine Monitor 2026 report recorded at least 6,929 people killed or injured by mines and explosive remnants in 2025, a 10% rise and the highest toll since 2020. Civilians accounted for 84% of known casualties, with children half of civilian victims whose ages were recorded. Myanmar had the most casualties; treaty withdrawals and renewed mine production are putting the international ban under pressure.

articles.title: ‘Hunger Games’ Is a Box Office Power Again Thanks to Haymitch Abernathy
articles.summary: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opened with about $120 million in North America and $225 million worldwide, giving Lionsgate one of its strongest debuts in more than a decade. The prequel centers on young Haymitch Abernathy and added roughly $12.8 million on Monday, according to TheWrap’s analysis. Its launch ranks among the top openings for franchise prequels, but the Thanksgiving frame brings new competition and final grosses remain subject to later reporting.

articles.title: “Only Path Forward Is to Abolish”: Outcry After Masked ICE Agents Arrest Family at Seattle Airport
articles.summary: Video of masked, plainclothes ICE agents arresting a father and daughter at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport prompted criticism from Washington officials. ICE said the father was targeted for overstaying a visa and that his daughter would face an assault charge; witnesses dispute the agency’s account of a coffee incident. The airline and airport authority said they had no advance knowledge of the operation, and both detainees remained in custody.

articles.title: Abercrombie raises annual sales, profit forecast on strong apparel demand
articles.summary: Abercrombie & Fitch lifted its annual sales and earnings forecasts after strong demand for Hollister and Abercrombie helped shares rise about 22% to a more than two-year high. Third-quarter sales increased 11% at Hollister and 12% at Abercrombie, while the company cited promotions and controlled inventory ahead of the holiday season. Freight costs remain a margin headwind, and retailers overall have reported mixed consumer demand.

articles.title: About 175 migrants missing after boat from Senegal loses contact
articles.summary: About 175 people are unaccounted for after a Europe-bound wooden boat left Dakar around November 9–10 and lost contact, local officials and a rights group told Reuters. Senegal’s navy says it has rescued or intercepted thousands of migrants this month, while more than 8,000 reached Spain’s Canary Islands in the first 12 days of November. The missing passengers’ fate remains unknown.

articles.title: Adani reportedly agrees to buy recycled copper from Attero
articles.summary: Sources told Reuters that Adani agreed to a three-year copper supply arrangement valued at approximately $1 billion at prevailing prices. Attero would recover copper from discarded electronics and batteries for Adani's Gujarat facility. The arrangement could reduce reliance on imported material as the smelter expands. Adani did not comment on the reported agreement.

articles.title: Airlines rethink aircraft financing as high fuel costs squeeze cash
articles.summary: Airlines are changing how they finance aircraft as jet fuel remains more than 50% above pre-war levels, Reuters reports. Some carriers are arranging financing for new-aircraft deposits or considering sale-and-leaseback deals to preserve cash, while testing scenarios with fuel near $200 a barrel in 2027. Higher fares and capacity cuts have not fully offset costs, and sale-and-leasebacks bring long-term lease obligations.

articles.title: Amtrak sets ridership record as rising gas prices encourage Americans to travel by rail
articles.summary: Amtrak recorded 37.1 million passengers in the year through September 30, up 7.4% and its third annual ridership record in a row. The railroad attributed part of the increase to higher fuel and airline prices, alongside improved Northeast Corridor infrastructure and newer trains. Revenue rose 4.9% to $4.1 billion, though it still reported an adjusted $492.7 million loss. A faster New York–Washington trip is targeted for 2028, subject to approvals.

articles.title: AP investigation: The DEA allowed 1.4 million fentanyl pills to go unseized in major probe
articles.summary: An Associated Press investigation found that DEA agents allowed at least 1.4 million additional fentanyl pills to move through six states while monitoring a trafficking network from August 2024 to April 2025. The agency says its tactics were lawful and coordinated with prosecutors; critics argue the delay exposed communities to lethal drugs. The findings have prompted congressional scrutiny and a New Mexico criminal investigation.

articles.title: Appeals court ends federal case over 20,000 California ballots
articles.summary: A federal appeals court approved the Justice Department’s request to dismiss its lawsuit over roughly 20,000 California ballots that it had sought to hold until officials checked recipients’ immigration status. The Ninth Circuit ruling ends that litigation after Election Day made the requested relief moot. The case formed part of a wider federal-state dispute over election administration; a separate voting-rights suit was also dismissed.

articles.title: Artists urge Australia to preserve copyright protections in AI legislation
articles.summary: More than 7,000 creatives, including Kate Bush and Grace Jones, have backed a campaign demanding permission-based use of their work for AI training. An Australian parliamentary committee has recommended measures to facilitate compensation for rights holders. Technology companies argue that existing licensing arrangements complicate model development, while industry representatives favor enforcing current protections. The recommendations are not yet government policy.

articles.title: BBC to trial CBeebies children's shows on Netflix in new partnership
articles.summary: The BBC will place a selection of CBeebies children’s programmes, including Hey Duggee and Teletubbies, in a branded Netflix hub in Britain beginning December 2. Reuters says the trial is part of the broadcaster’s effort to reach audiences on commercial platforms; iPlayer remains the home of the full CBeebies service. Netflix will also fund a small number of new commissions, with selected content distributed internationally.

articles.title: Brad Pitt, Quentin Tarantino and David Fincher reunite for Cliff Booth spinoff
articles.summary: Brad Pitt returns as stuntman Cliff Booth in The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, a spinoff written by Quentin Tarantino and directed by David Fincher. Reuters reports the story is set in 1977, eight years after Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood, and follows Booth as he helps people in the film industry. The movie opens globally in IMAX before arriving on Netflix December 23.

articles.title: Brazil crime-fighting AI startup Pax expanding to three more regions
articles.summary: Brazilian startup Pax is extending its AI-assisted police platform into three additional jurisdictions, adding pilots in Mato Grosso do Sul, Bahia and the Federal District. The system searches surveillance footage, dispatch calls and police records to help officers connect people, vehicles and evidence. Pax and a Goiás police official report faster case identification and improved clearance figures in one monitored area, but those results are company-specific and do not establish independent effectiveness elsewhere.

articles.title: Brazil zoo hails birth of Spix's macaw chick as boost for species' recovery
articles.summary: São Paulo Zoo announced the birth of a female Spix’s macaw named Hope, a milestone for a parrot classified as extinct in the wild. The chick hatched after a 28-day artificial incubation and required help from keepers. The species was driven to the brink by habitat loss and trapping; its future now depends on managed breeding and eventual conservation work beyond captivity.

articles.title: Canada pushes back against Pentagon criticism of defense spending
articles.summary: Canadian Defense Minister David McGuinty rejected Washington's criticism of Ottawa's military spending, emphasizing Canada's sovereignty. He said Canada plans to reach defense and related security spending of 5% of GDP by 2035, with an interim target of 4% by 2030. The Pentagon has questioned the pace of Canada's spending commitments.

articles.title: Car bomb in Colombia's Villavicencio injures 23 as violence spreads to cities
articles.summary: A bomb exploded outside regional government offices in Villavicencio, Colombia, injuring 23 people and damaging nearby buildings, the Associated Press reported. Authorities said the blast occurred Monday night and remained under investigation. The attack comes amid escalating clashes between security forces, rebel factions and drug gangs, which have increasingly used drones, rockets and roadside explosives. Officials have not established responsibility, and the investigation continues.

articles.title: Catalysts come alive as electron microscopy reveals nanoparticles’ dynamic behavior
articles.summary: Scientists at the universities of Nottingham and Cardiff tracked individual catalyst nanoparticles during a reaction that converts carbon dioxide and hydrogen into methanol. Electron microscopy revealed that particles move, merge and reorganize, while zinc oxide forms thin, porous shells that stabilize them without blocking reactions. The findings challenge the idea that catalysts remain static and could guide designs for more durable, efficient industrial processes.

articles.title: CDC director draws doubts from employees and ire from legislators
articles.summary: Three months into her tenure, CDC Director Erica Schwartz faces House Democratic investigations, calls to resign and low staff morale amid measles, dengue and Ebola outbreaks. The agency’s revised process for counting measles deaths has produced lower totals than states report, while employees question transparency and leadership stability. Schwartz says she is working to restore trust; Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. continues to back her.

articles.title: Chicago Cubs add LHP Trevor Rogers and Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, AP source says
articles.summary: Chicago’s Cubs agreed to a five-year, $120 million contract with left-handed pitcher Trevor Rogers and a deal with Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, according to an Associated Press source. Rogers adds a starter after a 10–11 season with Baltimore, while Sato arrives after winning Japan’s Central League Triple Crown and a second straight MVP. Both moves were pending physicals, and Sato’s strikeout rate is a question for MLB adjustment.

articles.title: China Southern orders 50 jets in Boeing's biggest China deal in nearly a decade
articles.summary: China Southern subsidiary Xiamen Airlines agreed to buy 50 Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft at a list price of about $7.4 billion, Reuters reports. Deliveries are scheduled for 2031–2034, making it the largest Chinese order for Boeing in nearly a decade. The purchase converts part of a 200-jet commitment announced at a U.S.-China summit, signaling a thaw in commercial aviation ties despite continuing trade tensions.

articles.title: China's Huawei convicted in sprawling US criminal trial over Iran business
articles.summary: A Brooklyn jury convicted Huawei on 10 of 12 federal counts, including bank fraud, wire fraud, sanctions violations and conspiracy to steal trade secrets, in a case stemming from the company’s Iran business and dealings with U.S. firms. Jurors rejected racketeering-conspiracy and obstruction counts. Huawei says it expects to appeal; sentencing is scheduled for September 2027, leaving penalties unresolved.

articles.title: Chinese researcher is in 'remarkable spirits' after ICE detention, professor says
articles.summary: Princeton neuroscience researcher Eva Yi Xie is being held in Virginia after immigration agents detained her at Reagan National Airport. Homeland Security says she overstayed her visa and lacked study authorization; her lawyer says a pending asylum application allows her to live and work in the U.S. A judge barred her removal from Virginia while reviewing a challenge to the detention, and Princeton colleagues are seeking answers.

articles.title: Climate scientists urge US lawmakers to vote no on sweeping permitting bill
articles.summary: More than 120 climate scientists urged the U.S. House to reject the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, arguing that its permitting changes could lock in fossil-fuel projects and weaken environmental safeguards. Supporters say the bill would speed clean-energy and transmission construction and reduce electricity costs. The Senate has passed it, and House lawmakers are considering amendments before a vote; the legislation’s effects remain contested.

articles.title: Daniels leads winning drive as Commanders walk off Bengals in thriller
articles.summary: Washington beat Cincinnati 22–20 after quarterback Jayden Daniels led a 64-yard drive in the final 34 seconds, setting up Drew Stevens’ 26-yard field goal as time expired. Daniels connected twice with rookie Antonio Williams after the Bengals had taken a one-point lead. The win kept Washington in the NFC East race and ended Cincinnati’s five-game winning streak. The Associated Press noted Washington’s six consecutive scoring drives of more than 50 yards.

articles.title: Democrats aim to reverse Trump's slashes to US food aid, but path unclear
articles.summary: Democratic leaders say they will seek to reverse $187 billion in food-assistance cuts when they take control of Congress in January. Reuters reports more than 5.5 million people have lost Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits since the 2025 tax law, while food banks report sustained demand. Democrats have not settled on a legislative route, and a veto threat means overriding the president would require broad Republican support.

articles.title: Dozens of oil and shipping tankers hacked in recent weeks, per report
articles.summary: TechCrunch reported, citing The Wall Street Journal, that U.S. officials suspect Iranian hackers may be behind as many as 50 recent cyberattacks on oil and shipping vessels. The targeted ships carried oil, liquefied gas and other hazardous cargo across Asia and Europe; earlier navigation-system breaches also prompted FBI and Coast Guard teams to board tankers near the U.S. The allegations have not been independently confirmed publicly.

articles.title: Draft Smithsonian overhaul plan prompts questions about White House influence
articles.summary: A Washington Post investigation reports that a photographed draft plan titled “Smithsonian Institution Renewal Plan” proposed sweeping changes to museum leadership, exhibitions, grants and internal policies. The document surfaced after a commuter photographed a White House aide working on it aboard the D.C. Metro. A Democratic lawmaker pledged oversight hearings, while Smithsonian leaders defended the institution’s independence and said the plan’s intended use was unclear.

articles.title: Elon Musk asks appeals court to overturn Twitter shareholder fraud verdict
articles.summary: Elon Musk asked a U.S. appeals court to overturn a jury verdict that found he defrauded Twitter shareholders by publicly questioning his 2022 takeover agreement. His lawyers argue investors did not prove his posts caused the stock decline and challenge the class-action certification. Reuters says the shareholders’ lawyers estimate damages could reach $2.6 billion plus interest if the verdict stands; the appeal remains unresolved.

articles.title: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life
articles.summary: A new ShellBench benchmark suggests that even leading AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta struggle with everyday tasks that require reliable judgment. The systems failed more than one-third of attempts, while 15.7% of all tested attempts violated at least one safety requirement, sometimes causing unintended consequences. The findings challenge claims that consumer agents are ready to manage shopping, travel and other personal responsibilities autonomously.

articles.title: FHFA raises 2027 conforming loan limit to $855,400 for most U.S. homes
articles.summary: The Federal Housing Finance Agency will let Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac buy or guarantee single-family mortgages up to $855,400 in most U.S. counties beginning in 2027, a 2.7% increase. Higher limits apply in expensive areas, including $1.28 million in Los Angeles County and $1.22 million in New York County. The change reflects rising home values, while elevated mortgage rates continue to weigh on sales.

articles.title: Five Turkish soldiers killed in helicopter crash, ministry says
articles.summary: Turkey’s Defence Ministry said five soldiers died when an AS-532 military helicopter crashed during a training flight in central Eskişehir province. The ministry did not disclose a cause, and Reuters reported no immediate details about weather, mechanical issues or an investigation. The incident adds to military aviation losses that can involve complex training and maintenance factors, but the available information does not establish what brought the aircraft down.

articles.title: French officials order former President Sarkozy's corruption case to trial
articles.summary: French authorities have sent a case involving former President Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife, Carla Bruni, to trial over alleged efforts to secure the retraction of testimony linking Sarkozy’s 2007 campaign to Libyan money. The witness, businessman Ziad Takieddine, later withdrew his account and has since died. Sarkozy and Bruni deny wrongdoing; the case is separate from his earlier Libya-financing conviction, which he is appealing. A pre-trial hearing is set for April 2027.

articles.title: Gavi plans to buy up to 1.5 million doses of experimental Ebola vaccine for Congo
articles.summary: Gavi plans to buy up to 1.5 million doses of an experimental vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola if trials in the Democratic Republic of Congo show it is safe and effective. The candidate was developed by Oxford and the Serum Institute of India. No licensed vaccine or treatment exists for this strain, which has caused a major outbreak; purchase terms were not disclosed.

articles.title: Gaza issues meningitis epidemic alert after infections surge
articles.summary: Gaza's health ministry reported 272 meningitis infections in October, more than eight times the usual monthly range, and issued an epidemic alert. Fifteen people have died since the start of 2026, according to the ministry. Aid agencies cite overcrowded shelters, sewage-contaminated water, damaged infrastructure and restricted supplies as contributing conditions. The figures include suspected cases, and independent verification is difficult amid the continuing humanitarian emergency.

articles.title: Gisèle Pelicot condemns publisher over use of intimate images in book promotion
articles.summary: Gisèle Pelicot criticized a Paris publisher for using intimate photographs taken by her former husband to promote a book about her rape case. Her lawyer said the images were part of evidence in the trial that convicted 51 men, including her ex-husband. The publisher apologized, halted promotion and said it would not print more copies, while disputing descriptions of the images as explicit.

articles.title: Holiday shoppers return to malls for in-person experiences
articles.summary: Retail surveys indicate renewed interest in physical shopping ahead of Thanksgiving. A JLL survey found approximately 55% of holiday shoppers intended to visit an indoor mall, compared with around half last year. Retailers are adding dining, customization and other experiences to attract visitors. The figures reflect shoppers' stated plans rather than final holiday sales.

articles.title: Hong Kong fire survivors mark one year amid grief and questions over accountability
articles.summary: One year after a fire killed 168 people across seven Hong Kong apartment blocks, survivors are still grieving and questioning accountability. An investigation cited unsafe maintenance work and weak oversight; prosecutions remain ongoing. Some residents say authorities have restricted public criticism and rejected rebuilding the complex. The anniversary has renewed scrutiny of the government’s response and the resettlement of displaced homeowners.

articles.title: House Democrat expands investigation into Donald Trump Jr.'s investment firm
articles.summary: House Judiciary Democrat Jamie Raskin requested two years of records from four companies linked to Donald Trump Jr.’s investment firm 1789 Capital, saying he is examining whether investments preceded favorable federal contracts or policy decisions. Trump Jr. and the firm deny wrongdoing, and companies gave varied responses. The inquiry could become a major oversight issue when Democrats take control of the House in January.

articles.title: Hungary, Ukraine make 'fresh start' as Magyar visit kickstarts trade talks
articles.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy called their meeting a fresh start and discussed trade, energy and rail links. Hungary had blocked parts of Ukraine’s EU accession process under former leader Viktor Orban; Magyar has eased some objections after Kyiv expanded language rights for minorities. No major deals were announced, but the visit signals warmer ties after years of friction.

articles.title: Iranian singer and four colleagues receive lashes, prompting criticism
articles.summary: Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her concert team each received 74 lashes in Qom, their lawyer told Iran International, after an online performance filmed without a live audience. The punishment prompted criticism from artists and activists and renewed scrutiny of restrictions on women singing publicly and compulsory-hijab rules. An appeals court had upheld their sentences in September, including bans on artistic activity and foreign travel.

articles.title: Israel's Eisenkot clinches first coalition agreement in bid to form government
articles.summary: Former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party agreed to its first coalition pact since the October election, joining with Avigdor Lieberman’s Israel Our Home party. Benjamin Netanyahu lost his parliamentary majority, but no rival bloc has yet secured a clear route to government. Reuters reports the agreement is an initial step rather than a completed coalition, with negotiations still needed to assemble a governing majority.

articles.title: Israeli airstrike kills senior Hamas security official in Gaza
articles.summary: An Israeli airstrike killed Naeem Abu Nahel, whom Palestinian officials identified as the head of Hamas’ internal security apparatus in Gaza, Reuters reports. Medics said at least six other Palestinians were killed in separate strikes, including police officers. Israel said it targeted militants; Hamas denied efforts to rearm and accused Israel of undermining the ceasefire. The attacks underscore that the 2025 truce has not ended violence in Gaza.

articles.title: Istanbul authorities reverse course on reported lioness
articles.summary: Authorities launched a day-long search after videos appeared to show a lioness in an Istanbul suburb. Residents were advised to remain indoors and a forest was closed. Officials subsequently said further images and field searches produced no evidence of a lion or other large feline. The animal’s actual identity remained unclear, prompting public confusion and jokes online.

articles.title: Japan looks to auto-parts suppliers to expand its defense industry
articles.summary: Japan is encouraging automotive component manufacturers to diversify into defense production as part of a broader security buildup. Reuters reports that procurement officials are connecting smaller suppliers with defense companies and funding opportunities. The initiative could create new markets for an auto industry facing declining domestic production. Major Japanese automakers have so far shown less interest than smaller suppliers.

articles.title: Libya's Tripoli government asks court to annul disputed Arkenu oil deal
articles.summary: Libya’s internationally recognised Tripoli government has asked a court to suspend and annul a production-sharing agreement with Arkenu Oil Company covering two major fields. A U.N. expert panel previously said the company moved more than $3 billion abroad; Arkenu disputes that characterization and says it operated under a valid state-backed contract. The dispute reflects continuing tensions over control and transparency in Libya’s oil sector.

articles.title: Life expectancy in Cuba falls for first time since 1950 amid economic crisis
articles.summary: World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said Cuba’s life expectancy fell from 78.8 years in 2020 to 74.4 in 2025, the first decline since records began in 1950. He also cited worsening infant and maternal mortality and lower childhood-cancer survival. The figures predate a U.S. fuel blockade imposed in January; the WHO chief pointed to both external sanctions and domestic economic problems.

articles.title: Major law firms recruit teams after Weil's dissolution
articles.summary: The dissolution of Weil, Gotshal & Manges has prompted intense competition for its approximately 1,200 attorneys. Reuters documents groups moving to firms including Gibson Dunn, Skadden and Kirkland & Ellis, with hiring spanning private funds, restructuring and litigation. Milbank is taking on the Paris team. The moves illustrate how the collapse is reshaping the market for legal talent.

articles.title: Martha Ford, former Lions owner with link to auto giants, dies at 101
articles.summary: Martha Firestone Ford, former principal owner of the Detroit Lions and a member of the Firestone and Ford families, has died at 101. She took control of the NFL team after her husband’s death in 2014 and led it until 2020, when her daughter succeeded her. Ford remained involved in Detroit civic and health organizations and attended Lions games into her final year.

articles.title: Meta launches Muse in UK – the AI agent that can do your Christmas shopping
articles.summary: Meta launched its Muse AI assistant in the UK, where users can connect selected apps and ask it to shop, book travel, manage calendars or draft messages. Meta says the agent cannot purchase items or send messages without approval and has no access to passwords or payment details. UK privacy and competition regulators are monitoring the rollout after reports of testing errors, including incorrect reminders and financial information.

articles.title: Mexico reports 12 active measles cases as vaccination coverage reaches 90%
articles.summary: Mexico reported 12 active measles cases, all in Chiapas, while its health minister said about 90% of the population was vaccinated and ten million doses were available. The Pan American Health Organization says sustained transmission has cost Mexico its measles-free status and that at least 95% two-dose coverage is needed to stop transmission. The country must show 12 months without spread to regain certification.

articles.title: Michigan drops plans to hire new AD Trev Alberts, faces $21 million payout
articles.summary: Michigan abandoned plans to hire Texas A&M athletic director Trev Alberts, potentially triggering more than $21 million in payments and a legal dispute. Alberts had signed a five-year agreement worth $3.2 million annually plus bonuses; the university cited an unacceptable background check. The decision adds to instability in Michigan’s athletic department as it seeks new leadership for its football program.

articles.title: Microsoft launches emergency engineering review after major outage
articles.summary: Internal memos reviewed by Reuters describe an urgent engineering overhaul following the November 12–13 disruption of Microsoft 365 services, including email and Teams. Microsoft attributed the outage to a Windows scalability flaw. Planned improvements include faster recovery, better traffic management and improved diagnostics. The company aims to resolve future worldwide incidents within an hour, a target rather than an achieved capability.

articles.title: More than 300 Russians killed as Moscow props up Mali’s junta, leaked data reveals
articles.summary: Leaked Russian state death records reviewed by the Guardian list 349 Russian fighters killed in Mali between September 2023 and September 2026, including 43 deaths on the day insurgents attacked Kidal in April. Western officials said the toll exceeded earlier estimates, though the records may be incomplete. The figures illuminate the human cost of Moscow’s support for Mali’s military government as insecurity has continued despite Russia’s growing role.

articles.title: Myanmar earthquake reveals how fault history could help anticipate future slip
articles.summary: Researchers used hundreds of supercomputer simulations and data from GPS, satellites, seismometers and video to study the magnitude 7.8 Myanmar earthquake in 2025. The models suggest that a fault’s history can help estimate likely slip patterns and rupture speed before a future quake. Scientists stress this is not precise earthquake prediction; the work aims to improve hazard assessment and rapid response.

articles.title: New workflow advances programmable chromosome editing in plants
articles.summary: A team at the Chinese Academy of Sciences published a protocol for programmable, large-scale chromosome editing in plants, enabling insertions, deletions, inversions and replacements across substantial DNA regions. The method combines engineered recombinases with prime editing and aims to remove leftover editing sequences. Researchers say the workflow could support crop breeding and synthetic biology, though edited plant lines still require validation and take months to produce.

articles.title: Pope Francis' private diary reveals spiritual doubts and a period of crisis
articles.summary: The Vatican released excerpts from Pope Francis’ private diary, spanning 1992 to August 2024, revealing spiritual doubts, health struggles and reflections on the clergy-abuse scandal. The notes describe a 2021–22 crisis that a close aide linked to Francis’ struggles with authority and governance. The book was curated by Cardinal Víctor Manuel Fernández, who says Francis wanted the writings published.

articles.title: Radar outage delays arrivals at Chicago O'Hare during Thanksgiving travel
articles.summary: A ground-surveillance radar outage at Chicago O’Hare delayed arrivals during one of the busiest Thanksgiving travel days, the FAA said. The agency warned that congestion could force another temporary halt to incoming flights; average delays reached 47 minutes, with some aircraft holding before landing. The incident added to a series of aviation technology disruptions, though officials expected technicians to restore the system overnight.

articles.title: Reported cyber breach affects unclassified U.S. intelligence data
articles.summary: A person familiar with the incident told Reuters that the CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence discovered unauthorized access to unclassified information. The affected network analyzes publicly available material. Officials said classified systems and essential capabilities had not been disrupted. The information exposed and the means of intrusion were not established in the report.

articles.title: Rope bridges help protect sloths from habitat loss in Costa Rica
articles.summary: Conservationists in Costa Rica have installed about 410 rope bridges to help sloths cross gaps in forest canopies fragmented by roads, hotels and development. The bridges reduce the need for the slow-moving animals to descend to the ground, where vehicles, dogs and power lines pose risks. Researchers say crossings and habitat corridors help, but long-term survival still depends on protecting and reconnecting forests.

articles.title: Santas and a polar bear emerge from washed-up container on Bulgarian beach
articles.summary: Bulgarian authorities found life-size Santa figures, a polar-bear statue and holiday decorations inside a shipping container washed ashore near Burgas. Officials suspect it may have come from the Greek cargo ship Contship Jet, which sank after a drone strike in October, but the vessel’s operator could not confirm the link. The container’s arrival highlights wider maritime-security concerns in the Black Sea as Russia’s war continues.

articles.title: Shein agrees to $100 million FTC settlement over shipping and review practices
articles.summary: Shein agreed to pay $100 million to settle U.S. Federal Trade Commission claims involving misleading shipping promises, filtered negative reviews and unsupported statements about cotton sourcing and supplier audits. The company did not admit liability and said it disagreed with some allegations. Reuters reports the settlement also requires changes to consumer practices, while the FTC says funds will be used to reimburse customers.

articles.title: South African court convicts man over plans to fight for Russia
articles.summary: A Zimbabwean man pleaded guilty in South Africa to violating legislation regulating foreign military assistance after agreeing to fight for Russia in Ukraine in exchange for payment. He received a suspended five-year sentence and faces deportation. The case comes amid wider concerns in several African countries about recruitment for the war and the treatment of recruits.

articles.title: South Korea issues alert after Russian warplanes enter air-defense zone near eastern island
articles.summary: Several Russian warplanes entered South Korea's air-defense identification zone near Ulleung Island, prompting Seoul to issue a brief public alert and summon Russia's military attaché. South Korea said the aircraft approached its territorial airspace but did not cross it; the alert was lifted after three minutes. Moscow said its aircraft acted within international law and disputes the legal basis of the zone. The incident followed other recent Russian aircraft entries.

articles.title: Spanish government challenges Madrid regional law extending rights to unborn children
articles.summary: Spain’s Socialist-led government said it will challenge a Madrid regional law that makes unborn children eligible for certain family benefits, including tax breaks and subsidies. Equality Minister Ana Redondo argues the measure conflicts with national law and could affect abortion rights; the regional government is led by the conservative People’s Party. The dispute is entering a national election campaign, while Madrid’s law remains regional and the Constitutional Court has yet to rule.

articles.title: Study compares AI's water use with almond milk and golf spending
articles.summary: An Enverus study reported by Reuters compares water use per dollar spent across activities, estimating that $25 of AI services consumes about 1.9 gallons, including water used to generate electricity. The report puts the same spending on almond milk at 308 gallons and golf at 679. The comparison depends on the study’s spending-based method and does not mean data centers have no local water impacts.

articles.title: Swedish parliament to vote on Moderates leader Kristersson to remain prime minister
articles.summary: Sweden’s parliament speaker nominated Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson for a November 30 confirmation vote, seeking to end a 72-day impasse after September’s election.
