His centre-right bloc lacks a majority, while centre-left parties have been unable to agree on a governing arrangement. The pivotal Centre Party has not chosen a side and rejects cooperation with both the Left Party and Sweden Democrats, leaving a fresh election possible if parliament cannot approve a prime minister.

articles.title: Thousands of Sikh pilgrims from India celebrate Guru Nanak’s 557th birthday in Pakistan
articles.summary: More than 5,000 worshippers gathered in Nankana Sahib, Pakistan, to mark the 557th birthday of Guru Nanak, Sikhism’s founder; officials said Pakistan issued more than 3,000 visas to Indian pilgrims. The gathering brought devotees from neighboring India to a major Sikh shrine despite strained India-Pakistan relations. Pilgrims are also scheduled to visit other sacred sites before returning home.

articles.title: Threads comes to iPad and adds cashtags for stock discussions
articles.summary: Meta has released an iPad version of Threads and added cashtags, which let users follow discussions tied to publicly traded companies. The tablet layout gives the social network more room for simultaneous conversations, while the stock tags borrow a feature popularized by X. The additions broaden Threads’ appeal beyond short text posts as Meta competes for users and financial discussion.

articles.title: Tidal bans 100% AI-generated music with plans to delete more than 27m tracks
articles.summary: Tidal says it will remove music it determines to be entirely AI-generated beginning December 9, a policy that could affect about 27 million tracks. The company said 43% of uploads in the previous 90 days were fully AI-generated and most received no streams. AI-assisted recordings remain eligible. The move is stricter than policies at Spotify and Apple Music and raises questions about how platforms will verify authorship.

articles.title: Trump nominates North Carolina prosecutor who lost re-election for federal judgeship
articles.summary: President Donald Trump nominated Jim O’Neill, a North Carolina district attorney who lost his November re-election bid, for a lifetime federal judgeship. The nomination is part of a push to confirm judicial candidates before Democrats take control of the Senate on January 3. O’Neill has served as Forsyth County district attorney since 2009; nineteen other nominees remain pending, according to Reuters.

articles.title: U2's new album is about 'defiant joy.' They'll tour it in North America next summer
articles.summary: U2 announced a 15-date North American stadium tour for 2027 following the release of its first album of new songs in nine years, “Carnaval de Luz.” The run begins in Miami in August and ends in Vancouver in October, with presales starting Nov. 30 and general sales Dec. 4. The band says the album and show emphasize collective celebration; drummer Larry Mullen Jr. has returned after surgery.

articles.title: Uber and Nuro begin driverless testing of Lucid robotaxis ahead of 2027 launch
articles.summary: Uber and autonomous-vehicle startup Nuro have begun testing driverless Lucid Gravity SUVs on public streets in the San Francisco Bay Area. The companies say employee rides will follow as they prepare a commercial robotaxi launch in the first quarter of 2027. The tests mark a step toward removing human safety drivers, but regulatory approvals, operational performance and public acceptance remain key hurdles.

articles.title: UK warns AI-driven cyberattacks are exposing years of weak security
articles.summary: The U.K. government’s cybersecurity unit says AI-assisted attacks have risen markedly, with hackers using autonomous tools to identify and exploit basic weaknesses in networks. Officials warn the technology can speed up intrusion attempts and expose long-standing security gaps, rather than relying only on novel vulnerabilities. The warning puts pressure on organizations to improve patching and basic defenses as AI-enabled tools become more accessible.

articles.title: UK warns of Russian sabotage threat to companies that supply Ukraine
articles.summary: Britain’s Ministry of Defence and MI5 warned companies supplying Ukraine’s military that they face heightened sabotage risks from Russian-linked operatives. The public alert cites arson and other low-tech tactics and follows suspected incidents across Europe. Russia denies plans to attack the United Kingdom and accuses Ukraine of staging sabotage. British officials are briefing defense and infrastructure firms on security precautions.

articles.title: UN estimates 47,000 women and girls were killed by partners or relatives in 2025
articles.summary: UNODC and UN Women estimate that 47,000 women and girls were killed by intimate partners or family members in 2025—about five every hour. These deaths represented roughly 60% of the 78,000 intentional killings of women and girls worldwide. Africa recorded the highest estimated rate, followed by the Americas, Oceania, Asia and Europe. The agencies say the figures show that homes and family relationships remain a major site of lethal violence.

articles.title: UN warns HIV infections could rise again as global funding falls
articles.summary: UNAIDS chief Winnie Byanyima warned that new HIV infections could begin rising in 2027 as international funding cuts and prevention-service closures threaten recent progress. New infections fell to 1.2 million last year, a record low, despite global HIV funding dropping nearly one-fifth. The warning is a forecast based on emerging signs; full data confirming a reversal are not yet available.

articles.title: Underwater robots reveal first salp species known to live exclusively in deep sea
articles.summary: Researchers using remotely operated underwater vehicles have formally described Vitreosalpa gemini, a glass salp found only in deep ocean waters. The gelatinous animal lives roughly 280 to 2,200 meters below the surface, where it feeds on detritus and tiny organisms rather than surface phytoplankton. Its unusual reproductive cycle and role in moving carbon to the seafloor add to evidence that deep-sea ecosystems remain poorly documented.

articles.title: US consumer confidence jumps to highest level in nearly two years
articles.summary: U.S. consumer confidence rose to 103.3 in November, its highest reading since January 2025, according to the Conference Board. Respondents were more positive about jobs and the economy, with the share calling jobs plentiful reaching a 19-month high. The improvement was concentrated among Democrats and independents, while Republican confidence slipped. Inflation expectations remained elevated at 4.5%, and economists cautioned that optimism may not translate into stronger spending.

articles.title: US farm secretary pledges to fight court order halting her religious emails
articles.summary: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said she will appeal a federal judge’s ruling limiting religious messages sent to USDA staff through her official account. Employees and their union argued that agency-wide Christmas and Easter emails promoted Christianity in a way that could pressure workers. The judge said Rollins must respect boundaries, including stopping such messages when asked. Rollins says she will fight the decision through the Supreme Court.

articles.title: US lawmakers question FAA rollout of AI-assisted air traffic planning tool
articles.summary: Two dozen House Democrats questioned the Federal Aviation Administration’s nationwide rollout of SMART, an AI-assisted air-traffic planning tool, after a major telecom outage disrupted flights. The system analyzes schedules, weather and airport capacity to flag potential conflicts, but does not control aircraft. Lawmakers say they have not seen enough validation or redundancy evidence; the FAA said it would respond directly to their questions.

articles.title: US to host Copa America for second successive tournament in 2028
articles.summary: CONMEBOL and CONCACAF said the United States will host the 2028 Copa América from June 9 to July 9, with 10 South American teams joined by six from North America, Central America and the Caribbean. The six CONCACAF entrants will qualify through the 2027 Gold Cup. It will be the U.S. third time hosting and second consecutive edition; host cities and venues have not yet been announced.

articles.title: Walmart teams up with Meta to bring Black Friday deals to AI agent Muse
articles.summary: Walmart is partnering with Meta to let shoppers use the Muse AI agent to find, compare and purchase Black Friday deals. Customers can describe what they want instead of navigating Walmart’s site directly, giving the retailer a new route into AI-assisted commerce. The move contrasts with Amazon’s efforts to restrict third-party agents from completing purchases, highlighting competing strategies for agent-based shopping.

articles.title: Wendy’s hit with US class action over menu pricing
articles.summary: A proposed U.S. class action accuses Wendy’s and restaurant-software provider NCR Voyix of using shared transaction data and centralized pricing to coordinate menu prices across franchises. The complaint was filed in Maryland and has not been proven in court. The companies had not responded to Reuters’ requests for comment at publication. The case adds to litigation challenging how retailers use algorithmic pricing tools and sales data.

articles.title: White House pardons two Thanksgiving turkeys
articles.summary: President Trump continued the annual Thanksgiving tradition by sparing two turkeys from West Virginia named Freedom and Feathers. Freedom attended the White House event after an online public vote. Both birds will retire at Texas A&M University. The ceremony became an annual presidential tradition during George H.W. Bush's administration in 1989.

articles.title: WHO chief urges US to lift Cuba fuel restrictions, warning of health effects
articles.summary: World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus urged the United States to lift its fuel restrictions on Cuba, warning that power shortages are harming hospitals and putting vulnerable people, including children, at risk. WHO pledged $2 million for immunization and medical equipment. Washington says food and medicine exports are exempt from sanctions; the wider effects of the fuel restrictions remain disputed.

articles.title: States sue HUD over rule that could end housing aid for mixed-status families
articles.summary: Twenty-one states and Pennsylvania’s governor sued HUD over a rule taking effect Dec. 14 that would end federal housing aid for an entire mixed-status household if any member lacks eligible immigration status. States say the change could displace U.S.-citizen children and families that previously received prorated assistance. HUD argues the rule enforces eligibility law and redirects limited funds; the court challenge will test that interpretation.

articles.title: College Football Playoff rankings put Georgia, Utah, Texas and Notre Dame in top four
articles.summary: The fourth College Football Playoff rankings placed Georgia, Utah, Texas and Notre Dame in the top four, with Tennessee rising from ninth to fifth after other contenders stumbled. Alabama fell to sixth and UCLA to ninth, while Wake Forest moved into the top ten. The committee’s list shapes the final selection race, with two more rankings releases scheduled before the playoff field is set.

articles.title: Spain extends bank tax and proposes tougher rules for consumer lending
articles.summary: Spain’s government extended its bank levy for another year, expecting about €1.4 billion for social housing and support for vulnerable tenants, and proposed new caps on some high-cost consumer loans. Consumer lending has reached a record €117.8 billion. Both measures still need parliamentary approval; banks have challenged the tax, and a possible conservative-led government after Sunday’s election could weaken or repeal it.

articles.title: HKU Scientists Uncover Hidden Leaf Dynamics That Could Improve Amazon Rainforest Carbon Uptake Estimates
articles.summary: Researchers from the University of Hong Kong and collaborators found that seasonal leaf loss, renewal and ageing in the Amazon canopy are largely missed by conventional satellite observations. Accounting for those changes altered modeled annual photosynthetic carbon uptake by 9.4%, about 1.42 billion tonnes of carbon. The study suggests rainforest carbon estimates may need refinement; it does not mean the forest’s actual uptake changed by that amount.

articles.title: In the United States, more than 2.2 Million Women Relied on Fertility Awareness-Based Methods for Pregnancy Prevention in 2022-2023, Higher Than Earlier Estimates
articles.summary: New Guttmacher Institute and University of Utah estimates suggest 7%–8% of U.S. contraceptive users aged 18–44 used fertility-awareness methods in 2022–23, representing more than 2.2 million people. The researchers say standard surveys undercount users who combine cycle tracking with condoms or other methods. The estimates cannot establish a nationwide rise after 2023, though several Mountain West states showed growth through 2026.

articles.title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy Type 2I/R9
articles.summary: The FDA approved Welgemda (ribitol) as the first treatment for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9, a rare inherited disorder linked to FKRP mutations. In a 112-person placebo-controlled study, patients showed improvements in walking speed and lung function at an interim analysis. The medicine is an oral solution for eligible adults and children weighing at least 30 kilograms; long-term outcomes and safety monitoring remain important.

articles.title: FDA Approves First New Hormone Therapy for Early-Stage Breast Cancer in More Than 20 Years
articles.summary: The FDA approved giredestrant, marketed as Wilserdly, for certain adults with early-stage estrogen-receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer after surgery. The agency said the daily oral hormone therapy is the first new treatment of its type for this setting in more than 20 years. Approval was based on a Phase 3 trial showing a 30% lower risk of invasive recurrence or death versus standard endocrine therapy; overall-survival follow-up continues.

articles.title: CMS Announces Lower Negotiated Prices for 13 High-Cost Drugs
articles.summary: CMS announced negotiated prices for 13 high-spending Medicare Part B and Part D drugs, projecting $9.2 billion in net savings, or 45%, once the prices take effect Jan. 1, 2028. The medicines treat conditions including cancer and psoriatic arthritis. The announcement expands the federal negotiation program to 37 drugs across three cycles; actual savings for individual patients will depend on coverage, use and out-of-pocket rules.

articles.title: BepiColombo spacecraft remains safe in Mercury orbit after software glitch
articles.summary: Europe’s and Japan’s BepiColombo spacecraft remains safe in a stable orbit around Mercury after a software glitch prematurely ended its first thruster burn. The maneuver delivered about 77% of the planned velocity change, but the European Space Agency says the mission remains on track for the two science orbiters to separate on December 9. Routine observations are expected to begin in April 2027.

articles.title: FCC plans vote to loosen local TV and radio ownership limits
articles.summary: The Federal Communications Commission plans to vote December 17 on replacing some local radio and television ownership limits with case-by-case reviews. Reuters reports the proposal would remove subcaps on AM and FM station ownership within local markets, while leaving restrictions on mergers among the four major broadcast networks unchanged. Supporters say broadcasters need scale to compete with streaming; critics warn consolidation could reduce local media diversity.

articles.title: Massachusetts sues to block ICE courthouse arrests without judicial warrants
articles.summary: Massachusetts Attorney General Andrea Joy Campbell sued to stop ICE from making civil immigration arrests in state courthouses without judicial warrants. She says more than 1,110 courthouse arrests have occurred since President Donald Trump took office, including 38 after a state law took effect November 3. The Department of Homeland Security defended the practice as efficient; the court has not ruled on the new case.

articles.title: Moscow accuses Estonia of hostile actions on 'verge of triggering open war'
articles.summary: Russia accused Estonia of actions “on the verge of triggering open war” after Tallinn said it would close road crossings with Russia for six months from December 1. Moscow alleged Estonia allowed Ukrainian drones to use its airspace and obstructed Russian shipping; Estonia rejected the claims and said it never permits its territory to be used for foreign military operations. NATO said it was monitoring the situation.

articles.title: New York's top court shields social media companies from liability in Buffalo mass-shooting case
articles.summary: New York's highest court ruled 4-3 that major social media companies cannot be held liable in a lawsuit alleging their platforms helped radicalize the gunman who killed 10 Black people at a Buffalo grocery store in 2022. The majority said the attack was not a foreseeable consequence of platform design choices, applying Section 230 protections. A dissent said a jury should hear the claims; families are considering further options.

articles.title: Paper wasps recognize faces in ways strikingly similar to humans
articles.summary: Cornell researchers report that female northern paper wasps recognize individual faces using a localized group of neurons with activity resembling face-selective cells in primate brains. Experiments found the neurons responded to forward-facing images of other wasps, not side views or other insects, and encoded distinctive facial markings. The study suggests similar neural solutions evolved independently in insects and primates; researchers say comparisons with related wasp species may clarify how social recognition develops.

articles.title: PBS examines why some dogs watch and react to television
articles.summary: A PBS NewsHour report examined why some dogs watch television, focusing on a viral children’s series featuring animated seals. Veterinary ophthalmologist Freya Mowat said dogs can distinguish some colors and may respond to high-contrast movement and animal images; her research also studies age-related retinal changes. Not every dog enjoys screens: barking, agitation or escape behavior can signal that viewing is stressful rather than calming.

articles.title: Records: Government, judge debated constitutional implications of searching Rep. Ilhan Omar's home
articles.summary: Newly unsealed filings show a magistrate judge required federal investigators to account for Rep. Ilhan Omar’s constitutional privileges before searching her Washington home in October. The documents describe a protocol for protecting material covered by the Speech or Debate Clause but reveal little about the underlying investigation. Omar has not been charged and denies wrongdoing; most of the warrant affidavit remains sealed.

articles.title: Russia's return to international sport faces European resistance ahead of LA 2028
articles.summary: Russia's bid to return to international sport is meeting resistance from European governments and federations, complicating qualifying events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Norway, Sweden and Poland have denied visas to Russian athletes, while some teams refuse to compete against them. The Court of Arbitration for Sport is considering a Russian appeal over participation conditions, with a ruling expected by December 15; federations retain authority over many events.

articles.title: War-related shipping disruption could put food aid for 7.3 million more people at risk, WFP warns
articles.summary: World Food Programme chief Luke Lindberg warned that conflict-related disruptions around the Black Sea, Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb could add $727 million to agency costs by mid-2027, threatening assistance for 7.3 million more people. The WFP has already cut its 2027 target from 110 million to 91 million recipients. A proposed humanitarian corridor for Russian and Ukrainian grain remains uncertain as attacks and shipping constraints persist.

articles.title: U.S. Senate panel investigates JD Vance's alleged role in Venezuelan oil deal
articles.summary: A Senate committee is examining whether Vice President JD Vance used his office to help commodities trader Vitol secure a lucrative Venezuelan oil contract. Senator Maggie Hassan requested records by Dec. 14 after Reuters reported a meeting with Vitol trader John Addison before the U.S. operation in Venezuela. Vance and Addison deny the meeting; flight records reportedly placed their aircraft at the same Montana airport.

articles.title: UN-backed talks extend AI killer robot discussions to 2028, no binding rules
articles.summary: UN-backed talks in Geneva ended with countries agreeing to continue work on lethal autonomous weapons for two more years and develop a possible accord by 2028. They did not commit to binding rules sought by the UN secretary-general and campaigners. Activists blamed major military powers for weakening the outcome; the International Committee of the Red Cross warned that autonomous weapons can behave unpredictably and urged human control over force.

articles.title: International UN talks on controlling use of autonomous weapons collapse
articles.summary: Negotiations in Geneva failed to secure a mandate for talks on a legally binding treaty governing autonomous weapons, after Russia objected and the UN forum’s consensus rule prevented agreement. More than 100 countries had backed stronger rules, while the United States and several other military powers favored nonbinding measures or reliance on existing law. Delegates adopted a weaker mandate to continue discussions, leaving regulation unresolved as such systems are already being developed and used.

articles.title: US pursuit of ‘Trump-class’ warships has blown cost of new fleet by billions, report warns
articles.summary: The Congressional Budget Office estimates the Navy’s 30-year shipbuilding plan will cost about $54 billion annually, 18% above Navy projections, with 15 proposed Trump-class battleships a major contributor. The report questions whether concentrating firepower in a few large vessels fits the Navy’s stated strategy. At the same time, the Iran war has extended deployments, delayed maintenance and strained readiness across the fleet.

articles.title: Denmark to expel Russian diplomat over alleged plot to kill US-Ukrainian rapper
articles.summary: Denmark said it would expel Russia’s defence attaché after police said they had disrupted an alleged Russian intelligence plot to kill US-Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner before a September concert. Three suspects were arrested near the venue with firearms and knives, and a fourth was later detained; all denied wrongdoing. Moscow rejected the accusation, while Copenhagen said it was also considering tighter visa restrictions for Russian nationals.

articles.title: French police officers found guilty of racist assault on black music producer
articles.summary: Three French police officers were convicted of intentional group violence, with racism treated as an aggravating factor, after beating music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020. Security-camera footage contradicted their account that Zecler had attacked them; the officers were also found guilty of falsifying an official report. They received prison sentences of one to two years, partly suspended, and were barred from police service for life.

articles.title: Man accused of sparking deadly Los Angeles wildfire found guilty
articles.summary: A federal jury convicted former Uber driver Jonathan Rinderknecht of arson charges tied to the January 2025 Palisades fire, which killed 12 people and destroyed thousands of homes and businesses. Prosecutors said he ignited a brush fire whose embers later reignited in powerful winds; Rinderknecht maintained his innocence and suggested fireworks caused the blaze. He remains in custody and faces a possible sentence of five to 40 years.

articles.title: A cyberattack using artificial intelligence targeted the EU in October, official says
articles.summary: The European Commission confirmed that an AI-assisted cyberattack targeting an EU institution was detected on October 22 and remained under investigation nearly a month later. Officials said several applications were temporarily taken offline and most have since been restored; they reported no evidence of a broad staff data breach. The attackers and full operational impact were not disclosed, leaving important questions about the intrusion unresolved.

articles.title: South Korea becomes fourth country globally to hit $1 trillion exports on AI chip boom
articles.summary: South Korea’s exports passed $1 trillion for 2026, making it the fourth country to reach the milestone after Germany, the United States and China. Semiconductor shipments, driven by global AI investment, rose 184% in the first three quarters and represented 42% of exports. Reuters noted weak domestic demand and inequality remain concerns, prompting the government to plan a large fund for growth industries, young people and regional development.

articles.title: Record profits but record outflows: 'Sell Korea' trade stalks Seoul market
articles.summary: South Korea’s KOSPI has fallen 44% from its June record despite record AI-driven profits at Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, erasing about 3.3 quadrillion won in market value. Reuters reported foreign investors were on track for a seventh consecutive month of net selling, with $115.2 billion in cumulative outflows. Analysts said waning confidence in debt-funded AI infrastructure and fading buybacks have left few buyers.
